456. ## Controls
457. 
458. | Input | Action |
459. | --- | --- |
460. | `WASD` / arrow keys | Move, navigate, and cycle valid Battle targets |
461. | `Space` / `Enter` | Confirm, interact, or disarm a detected adjacent trap |
462. | `M` | Open the world or city map |
463. | `E` | Open hero equipment |
464. | `P` | Open party management after recruiting a companion |
465. | `C` | Open the Codex after its first discovery |
466. | `Y` | Open Achievements after the first natural unlock |
467. | `K` | Open the Gathering record after discovering a gathering discipline |
468. | `V` | Open Crafting after learning a non-starting recipe |
469. | `Q` | Open the quest journal after a quest starts |
470. | `T` | Mount or dismount after owning a mount |
471. | `F1` | Open or close Tips |
472. | `Esc` | Close the active overlay or skip an active cutscene |
473. | Mouse / touch | Select buttons and scroll lists |
474. 
475. Standard gamepads use the left stick or D-pad to move and navigate, `A` to
476. confirm, `B` to cancel, `X` to interact, `Y`/Menu to open the menu, View to open
477. Tips, bumpers to cycle Battle targets/pages, and triggers to scroll the Battle
478. log. The right stick moves a visible cursor so every pointer-first button remains
479. reachable; press the right stick to click it. Touch devices receive a
480. safe-area-aware D-pad plus A/B, Menu, Party,
481. and Tips controls; movement and action buttons support simultaneous touches.
482. Progression-specific touch actions remain hidden until their feature is
483. discovered.
484. Character and inventory search text fields open a native mobile text-entry
485. surface.
486. 
487. The `Esc` menu is data-driven. Resume, Inventory, Tips, Settings, and
488. save/title controls are always available; quests, Chronicle, Codex,
489. Achievements, Gathering, Crafting, Party, social details, mounts, and nautical
490. controls appear only after authoritative gameplay evidence reveals them.
491. Inventory remains usable before companion recruitment.
492. Advanced Tips unlock automatically as relevant progression is reached. In the
493. inventory view, arrows and Page Up/Down navigate, `R` cycles sorting, `F` cycles
494. filters, `/` focuses search, `X` transfers, and `Tab` changes the target. `T`
495. remains mount control. Settings can force touch visibility, swap left/right
496. touch layout, and choose automatic or fixed prompt sources. Mappings are stable
497. and intentionally not user-remappable; a partial remapper would leave
498. pointer-first and text-entry flows inaccessible.
499. 
500. Crafting uses Up/Down and Page Up/Down for recipes, Left/Right for batch size,
501. `Q`/`E` for categories, `R` for sorting, `F` for mobile-safe search, and `Tab`
502. for explicit hero/companion ownership. Pointer, touch, and the gamepad cursor
503. share the same buttons.
504. 
505. In the Codex, `1`-`6` or `Q`/`E` change categories, `/` opens accessible search,
506. `F` cycles the monster-family filter or knowledge discovery grouping, and `R`
507. cycles the active category's sort. Family completion and all category counts are
508. derived rather than persisted. Touch opens the Codex from the Esc menu, while a
509. gamepad can use the same menu and right-stick cursor; `X` opens Codex search
510. and `A` submits the shared text-entry form.

1. # Inventory presentation
2. 
3. ## Ownership and presentation
4. 
5. Hero and companion item ownership remains in each actor's canonical
6. `inventory` array. Equipment fields continue to reference the exact owned item
7. objects. Inventory presentation is derived by `src/systems/inventory.ts` and
8. must never sort, splice, or replace the canonical array.
9. 
10. Presentation preferences use the separate `2dnd_inventory_prefs` local-storage
11. key:
12. 
13. - sort: type, value, rarity, recent acquisition, or name
14. - filter: all, equipment, consumables, quest items, or crafting items
15. - search text
16. 
17. Recent acquisition is the reverse of canonical append order, so it requires no
18. ownership metadata or save-schema migration. Future crafting items use the
19. `crafting` item type and already participate in selectors and generated visuals.
20. 
21. ## Party and menu access
22. 
23. Press `P` to open party management, then select **Items**. The `Esc` menu also
24. opens the same Party & Inventory surface directly. `T` remains reserved for
25. mount control.
26. 
27. Inventory controls:
28. 
29. | Input | Action |
30. | --- | --- |
31. | `Up` / `Down` | Move the stable item selection |
32. | `Page Up` / `Page Down` | Move one visible page |
33. | `Home` / `End` | Select the first or last result |
34. | `Enter` | Use, equip, or inspect the selected item |
35. | `X` | Transfer the selected item to the current target |
36. | `R` | Cycle sort mode |
37. | `F` | Cycle filter |
38. | `/` | Focus search; `Enter` finishes typing |
39. | `Tab` | Cycle the party target |
40. 
41. Every action is also available through pointer buttons. The manager exposes
42. semantic inventory actions so future gamepad and mobile controls can invoke the
43. same behavior without emulating keyboard keys.
44. 
45. ## Restrictions
46. 
47. - Equipped items cannot transfer.
48. - Key items and mounts remain hero-owned.
49. - Equipment actions target the owning actor.
50. - Consumables use the existing validated target and consumption rules.
51. - Sorting, filtering, and search return entries with their original inventory
52.   indexes, so duplicate items and equipment links remain stable.
53. 
54. Generated item visuals are drawn procedurally from item type and rarity; no
55. external assets are used.
56.

2. name: save-system
3. description: Manage 2D&D save schema v17, migration, normalization, and location recovery
4. license: MIT
5. ---
6. 
7. # Save System
8. 
9. Game state is stored in `localStorage` by `src/systems/save.ts`. Shared audio
10. and accessibility preferences plus inventory presentation preferences are
11. stored separately.
12. 
13. ## Storage keys
14. 
15. - `2dnd_save`: game state
16. - `2dnd_preferences`: versioned audio and accessibility preferences
17. - `2dnd_inventory_prefs`: inventory sort, filter, and search presentation
18. 
19. Legacy `2dnd_audio_prefs` and `2dnd_cutscene_accessibility` values migrate into
20. `2dnd_preferences`. Inventory recency derives from reverse canonical append
21. order. Do not add presentation fields to item ownership or increment the
22. campaign schema for these preferences.
23. 
24. ## Current schema
25. 
26. `SAVE_VERSION` is 17.
27. 
28. ```typescript
29. interface SaveData {
30.   version: number;
31.   player: PlayerState;
32.   defeatedBosses: string[];
33.   codex: CodexData;
34.   appearanceId: string;
35.   timestamp: number;
36.   timeStep?: number;
37.   weatherState?: WeatherState;
38. }
39. ```
40. 
41. `Set<string>` values are serialized as arrays and reconstructed by the scene
42. loading path.
43. 
44. ```typescript
45. interface CodexData {
46.   entries: Record<string, CodexEntry>;
47.   unlockedEntryIds: string[];
48. }
49. ```
50. 
51. Monster entries retain defeat, AC, drop, and elemental discovery. Knowledge
52. IDs are normalized against `CODEX_KNOWLEDGE_ENTRIES`; completion and counts are
53. derived.
54. 
55. ## Player persistence
56. 
57. Important composed fields:
58. 
59. ```typescript
60. interface PlayerPosition {
61.   x: number;
62.   y: number;
63.   chunkX: number;
64.   chunkY: number;
65.   inDungeon: boolean;
66.   dungeonId: string;
67.   dungeonLevel: number;
68.   inCity: boolean;
69.   cityId: string;
70.   cityChunkIndex: number;
71. }
72. 
73. interface PlayerProgression {
74.   openedChests: string[];
75.   collectedTreasures: string[];
76.   exploredTiles: Record<string, boolean>;
77.   discoveredCities: string[];
78.   quests: QuestLogState;
79.   seenCutsceneIds: CutsceneId[];
80.   pendingCutsceneIds: CutsceneId[];
81.   skillChecks: Record<string, SkillCheckRecord>;
82.   trapSeed: number;
83.   trapStates: Record<string, TrapState>;
84.   trapGuidance: boolean;
85.   tutorial: TutorialProgress;
86.   worldEvents: WorldEventState;
87.   social: SocialState;
88.   achievements: AchievementState;
89.   gathering: GatheringState;
90.   crafting: CraftingState;
91.   nautical: NauticalState;
92.   discoveredFeatureIds: FeatureId[];
93.   pendingFeatureRevealIds: FeatureId[];
94.   debugDiscoveredFeatureIds: FeatureId[];
95.   debugSuppressedFeatureIds: FeatureId[];
96. }
97. 
98. interface QuestProgress {
99.   status: "locked" | "active" | "completed";
100.   stage: number;
101.   objectives: Record<string, number>;
102.   claimedRewards: string[];
103. }
104. 
105. interface QuestLogState {
106.   quests: Record<QuestId, QuestProgress>;
107.   seenWarnings: string[];
108. }
109. ```
110. 
111. `PlayerState.activeEffects` persists normalized `ActiveStatusEffect` values.
112. Codex entries persist `discoveredElements`. `PlayerState.party` persists unique
113. companion states, active order, independent progression/inventories/equipment,
114. control modes, dialogue state, and gambits. Quest progress stores status, stage,
115. objective counters, claimed reward IDs, and acknowledged danger warnings.
116. `seenCutsceneIds` stores stable completed-or-skipped story presentation IDs.
117. `pendingCutsceneIds` stores queued IDs awaiting completion or skip and is saved
118. before presentation. Replay changes neither collection; campaign completion
119. remains derived from quest state.
120. `tutorial.completed` prevents the new-player tutorial from reopening
121. automatically after completion or skip. Tutorial replay does not reset it.
122. Fixed non-combat checks persist the
123. ability, natural roll, modifier, repaired total, DC, outcome, and optional
124. choice ID.
125. `worldEvents` persists a stable seed, deterministic roll/cooldown counters, one
126. pending choice or special battle, idempotent resolved/claimed IDs, repeat
127. counters, and the bounded chronological World Events record.
128. `social` persists bounded alignment axes, per-town/per-faction reputation
129. scores, stable applied source IDs, and at most 40 recent cause entries. Names,
130. tiers, thresholds, shop modifiers, Codex milestones, and achievement hooks are
131. derived.
132. `achievements` persists earned records, once-only event counters/IDs, explicit
133. defeat-history validity, unlocked/equipped cosmetic titles, debug suppression,
134. and pending notice IDs. Definitions, categories, points, totals, and
135. reconstructable progress are derived from canonical data.
136. `gathering` persists a deterministic seed, stable node cooldown/depletion,
137. discovered node/resource IDs, once-only claimed outcomes, discipline statistics,
138. bounded history, and one exact pending minigame or guarded Battle outcome.
139. `crafting` persists known recipe IDs, stable applied discovery/transaction IDs,
140. natural craft and equipment-upgrade statistics, per-recipe counts, bounded
141. recent history, and the next sequence. Recipe definitions and values are
142. canonical derived data.
143. `nautical` persists boat ownership/condition/upgrades/cosmetics, discovered
144. ports/routes/islands/continents/sea tiles, bounded navigation statistics, and
145. recoverable pending merchant routes, hazards, and encounters. Continents, sea
146. zones, ports, routes, islands, boats, and encounter pools remain canonical data.
147. Feature discovery persists only stable revealed IDs, pending one-time feedback,
148. marked debug reveals, and debug-suppressed evidence. Availability is reconciled
149. from authoritative gameplay state and never controls that state.
150. 
151. ## Loading and migration
152. 
153. Treat parsed JSON as `unknown`. Use typed record guards and normalization
154. helpers; do not cast unvalidated nested values directly.
155. 
156. `loadGame()` currently handles:
157. 
158. - Legacy `bestiary` to `codex`
159. - Legacy flat player position fields to `player.position`
160. - Legacy flat progression fields to `player.progression`
161. - Schema-v3 skill-check progression to default quest + skill-check state
162. - Flat Ashen Road/Warden's Dispatch and recruitment progress to nested
163.   Twelvefold Covenant state without replaying completed rewards
164. - Schema-v3/v4 progression to schema-v5 explicit trap state
165. - Missing equipment, talents, abilities, rests, bank, mount, and appearance
166.   fields
167. - Missing/invalid active status effects
168. - Missing/invalid party state and gambit rules
169. - Missing, malformed, duplicate, unknown, or already-seen cutscene queue entries
170.   through `normalizeSeenCutsceneIds()` and `normalizePendingCutsceneIds()`
171. - Completed-but-unseen legacy epilogue recovery without deriving every
172.   historically eligible campaign scene
173. - Missing/invalid Codex elemental discoveries
174. - Missing, malformed, unknown, or duplicate Codex knowledge IDs
175. - Schema-v9 monster-only Codex migration plus idempotent recovery from durable
176.   city, dungeon, item, quest, and cutscene evidence
177. - Missing, malformed, or unknown quest entries through `normalizeQuestLog()`
178. - Missing/invalid non-combat skill-check records
179. - Missing/invalid trap seed, state, and guidance fields
180. - Missing/invalid tutorial completion state through
181.   `normalizeTutorialProgress()`
182. - Missing/invalid World Event state through `normalizeWorldEventState()`;
183.   malformed seeds clear pending encounters, unknown events/choices are removed,
184.   and records are bounded
185. - Missing/invalid social state through `normalizeSocialState()`; unknown town
186.   and faction IDs are removed, scores are clamped, applied IDs are deduplicated,
187.   and history is validated against those IDs
188. - Missing/invalid achievement state through `normalizeAchievementState()`;
189.   unknown/duplicate IDs are removed, counters/order are repaired, title
190.   cross-fields are validated, and schema-v12 or older saves reconcile durable
191.   milestones silently while retaining unknown defeat history
192. - Missing/invalid gathering state through `normalizeGatheringState()`; schema-v13
193.   saves gain defaults, malformed seeds clear generated node/pending state, and
194.   pending outcome/resource/pattern/location cross-fields are validated
195. - Missing/invalid crafting state through `normalizeCraftingState()`; schema-v14
196.   saves gain defaults, unknown/duplicate IDs are removed, statistics are clamped,
197.   history is bounded/resequenced, and durable discovery is reconciled
198. - Missing/invalid nautical state through `normalizeNauticalState()`; schema-v15
199.   and older saves gain defaults, unknown IDs and malformed pending records are
200.   removed, condition/statistics are clamped, and invalid sea positions recover
201.   to a safe port without losing other progression
202. - Missing, malformed, duplicate, or unknown feature IDs through
203.   `normalizeFeatureDiscoveryProgress()`; schema-v16 and older saves discard
204.   pending/debug metadata and silently reconcile mature authoritative evidence
205. - Missing time and weather data
206. - Invalid string arrays and explored-tile records
207. 
208. ## Location recovery
209. 
210. After migration, normalize location state:
211. 
212. 1. Dungeon and city flags are mutually exclusive.
213. 2. Unknown dungeon/city IDs are cleared.
214. 3. Dungeon levels and city district indexes are clamped.
215. 4. Coordinates must be in bounds and walkable on the resolved level/chunk.
216. 5. Invalid interior coordinates move to that level/district spawn.
217. 6. Invalid overworld chunks/tiles fall back to the Willowdale start at chunk
218.    `(4, 2)`, tile `(3, 3)`.
219. 
220. Always resolve maps through `getDungeonLevelMap()` and `getCityChunk()` during
221. validation.
222. 
223. ## Adding or changing persistent data
224. 
225. 1. Update the TypeScript interface.
226. 2. Set the creation default.
227. 3. Normalize the loaded value from `unknown`.
228. 4. Validate cross-field invariants.
229. 5. Increment `SAVE_VERSION` for a schema change.
230. 6. Add tests for valid persistence, missing values, malformed values, and
231.    corrupt-location recovery.
232. 7. Update README and repository instructions when the stored shape changes.
233. 
234. For party data, normalize after quests, skill checks, and trap fields. Then
235. replay completed `recruitCompanion` quest actions so v5 saves and debug-completed
236. quests converge idempotently.
237. 
238. Normalize seen and pending cutscene IDs on every load against `CUTSCENE_IDS`.
239. Unknown IDs are discarded, IDs remain stable after release, and pending IDs
240. already present in the seen list are removed. Missing lists default to empty;
241. legacy recovery may queue only the completed-but-unseen epilogue.
242. 
243. Pre-v9 saves did not have tutorial state and normalize to `completed: true` so
244. existing campaigns are not interrupted. New v9 players start false; malformed
245. v9 values also normalize safely to false.
246. 
247. Do not silently retain malformed data. Use a safe default or reject the save
248. when the top-level payload is unusable.
249. 
250. ## Status and element rules
251. 
252. - Normalize status IDs, integer durations, and sources with
253.   `normalizeActiveEffects()`.
254. - Filter Codex element values with `isElement()`.
255. - Unknown values are discarded rather than asserted into the target type.
256. 
257. ## Skill-check rules
258. 
259. - Normalize with `normalizeSkillCheckRecords()`.
260. - Accept only Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma records with integer
261.   d20 rolls, modifiers, and positive DCs.
262. - Recompute `total` and `success` from the saved natural roll, modifier, and DC.
263. - Trim optional choice IDs and discard malformed records.
264. - Shop, NPC, chest, and treasure IDs must remain stable across content changes.
265. 
266. ## API
267. 
268. ```typescript
269. saveGame(player, defeatedBosses, codex, appearanceId, timeStep, weatherState);
270. const save = loadGame();
271. hasSave();
272. deleteSave();
273. getSaveSummary();
274. ```
275. 
276. Save failures are reported with `debugLog()`. Loading returns `null` when the
277. top-level save is absent or corrupt.
278. 
279. ## Tests
280. 
281. `tests/save.test.ts` covers:
282. 
283. - Save/load round trips
284. - Seen/pending cutscene round trips, malformed queue repair, and legacy epilogue
285.   recovery
286. - Legacy flat-state migration
287. - Current schema-v17 position, objective/reward/warning quest state, skill checks,
288.   traps, party state, pending cutscene queue, tutorial completion, and World
289.   Event recovery, plus alignment/reputation round trips and corruption repair
290. - Flat schema-v4 quest migration and completed-reward preservation
291. - Schema-v3 skill-check saves gaining default normalized quest state
292. - Schema-v4 quest saves gaining default trap state
293. - Schema-v5 party defaults plus all-three completed recruitment replay after
294.   malformed duplicate/unknown party entries are normalized
295. - Quest reward and skill-check record normalization
296. - Trap seed/state/guidance normalization and seed-state cross-field repair
297. - Dungeon-level and city-district clamping
298. - Invalid IDs and coordinates
299. - Conflicting location flags
300. - Status-effect persistence and normalization

7. # Testing Guide for 2D&D
8. 
9. Write comprehensive game-mechanics tests with Vitest. Use the committed
10. Playwright suite only for high-value Phaser browser flows that cannot be proven
11. through pure logic tests.
12. 
13. ## Testing Philosophy
14. 
15. ### What TO Test
16. ✅ Dice probability distributions
17. ✅ Combat calculation accuracy  
18. ✅ Group initiative, formation, targeting, synergies, rewards, and encounter budgets
19. ✅ Player stat progression
20. ✅ XP and leveling formulas
21. ✅ Quest objective counters, prerequisites, rewards, gates, danger rules, and
22. save normalization
23. ✅ Companion definitions, party progression, transfers, KO/reward rules, and
24. ranked gambit selection/normalization
25. ✅ Data integrity (monsters, spells, items)
26. ✅ Monster family references, membership, variant differentiation, palette
27. uniqueness, encounter weights, Codex family completion, and texture-key coverage
28. ✅ Codex knowledge IDs, canonical references, every unlock signal, idempotency,
29. normalization/migration, search/sort/group behavior, and future-hook isolation
30. ✅ Game logic functions
31. ✅ Seeded layouts and persistent state machines
32. ✅ Non-combat skill-check math, outcomes, and save normalization
33. ✅ Scene-transition event ordering, duplicate guards, and watchdog recovery with
34. mocked camera/time adapters
35. ✅ Cutscene data integrity, trigger priority, queue recovery, replay immutability,
36. shared preference normalization/migration, and director cleanup
37. ✅ Runtime hero descriptor normalization, collision-free visual keys, every
38. cutscene hero-role cue, equipment layer ordering/fallbacks, texture leases, and
39. current-player rendering across opening, recovery, Chronicle, bosses, and ending
40. ✅ Tutorial content integrity, semantic control references, completion
41. normalization, progression-aware tip unlocks, and save migration
42. ✅ Feature registry integrity, authoritative reconciliation, irreversible
43. visibility, dynamic menu/tab filtering, focus clamping, shortcut/touch gating,
44. debug exclusion, category-specific discovery, and schema-v17 migration
45. ✅ Defeat penalty receipts, once-only Battle resolution, recovered save
46. round-trips, result-scene continuation, and random/boss parity
47. ✅ Animation state selection, reduced-motion timing, stable actor/target mapping,
48. once-only completion and cleanup, and family-frame fallback resolution
49. ✅ Semantic mappings, context priority, analog dead zones, repeats, source
50. switching, duplicate suppression, disconnect/blur cleanup, and control
51. preference migration
52. ✅ Measured stacks/grids, safe-area clamping, long-string wrapping,
53. pagination/visible ranges, filtered focus restoration, scaled bounds,
54. hit-area alignment, and debug/test overlap detection
55. ✅ Alignment boundaries, reputation tiers, clamping, stable-source
56. idempotency, quest/dialogue/event/trap/combat hooks, shop composition, Codex
57. milestones, schema-v12 migration, bounded history, and debug commands
58. ✅ Achievement definition integrity, deterministic progress, hidden entries,
59. idempotent battle/event/social hooks, reconciliation, schema-v13 migration,
60. one-hit/no-defeat rules, cosmetic titles, debug exclusion, notices, and
61. authority isolation
62. ✅ Gathering terrain safety, seeded tables, all three state machines,
63. reduced-motion equivalence, cooldowns, environmental weights, economy, guarded
64. Battle handoffs, recipe-input isolation, schema-v14 migration, and pending reload
65. ✅ Crafting recipe integrity, alternative material matching, protected/equipped
66. items, atomic batches, repeated-input suppression, equipment-link upgrades,
67. ownership, discovery, acquisition tables, anti-arbitrage, achievements, debug
68. exclusion, authority isolation, schema-v15 migration, and corruption repair
69. ✅ Nautical continent/zone/port/island integrity, pre-boat merchant routes,
70. boat acquisition/upgrades, embark/disembark safety, sea fog, capped encounters,
71. weather hazards, Kraken hooks, sea gathering/crafting economy, schema-v16
72. migration/corruption recovery, debug commands, and browser reload while sailing
73. 
74. ### What NOT to Test  
75. ❌ Phaser rendering/graphics
76. ❌ Scene transitions
77. ❌ User input handling
78. ❌ Visual appearance
79. ❌ Animation timing
80. 
81. These exclusions apply to Vitest. The focused `e2e/` suite owns the real-browser
82. campaign golden path and scene/input integration.
83. 
84. Animation browser coverage should assert debug-state evidence from real action
85. menus and combat turns for hero, companion, monster, and boss presentation;
86. spell/ability particles; world/follower/mount gait; boss cutscenes; fainting;
87. reduced-motion immediate states; and page/console cleanliness.
88. 
89. Battle backdrop browser coverage uses deterministic `/battleview` and
90. `/backdrop` controls, programmatic depth/bounds/cleanup assertions, and focused
91. canvas screenshots for group, boss, Kraken, mobile, weather, and high-contrast
92. combinations. Keep the full biome/time/weather matrix assertion-driven rather
93. than committing hundreds of redundant images.
94. 
95. Accessibility browser coverage should change settings from both title and
96. in-game surfaces, assert immediate canvas state, exercise core overlays at every
97. supported text scale, verify reload persistence, and prove `2dnd_save` is
98. unchanged by preference updates.
99. 
100. Semantic-controls browser coverage uses mobile/touch emulation and deterministic
101. standard-gamepad stubs. It covers onboarding and mobile text entry, movement,
102. overlays, prompt/source switching, Battle action/target confirmation, defeat
103. recovery, gamepad cursor visibility, portrait/landscape layout, and page/console
104. cleanliness.
105. 
106. Codex browser coverage follows real exploration, quest, cutscene, item, NPC, and
107. readable paths; verifies non-blocking feedback, reload persistence, schema-v9

111. ## Test File Organization
112.

146. Quest tests must cover duplicate matching monsters in one group victory,
147. durable boss reconciliation, optional-objective reward cutoffs, hard-gate

6. 
7. # Phaser 4 Scene Management
8. 
9. ## Scenes and keys
10. 
11. | File | Class | Scene key |
12. | --- | --- | --- |
13. | `Boot.ts` | `BootScene` | `BootScene` |
14. | `Overworld.ts` | `OverworldScene` | `OverworldScene` |
15. | `Battle.ts` | `BattleScene` | `BattleScene` |
16. | `Shop.ts` | `ShopScene` | `ShopScene` |
17. | `Codex.ts` | `CodexScene` | `CodexScene` |
18. | `Cutscene.ts` | `CutsceneScene` | `CutsceneScene` |
19. | `Ending.ts` | `EndingScene` | `EndingScene` |
20. | `Defeat.ts` | `DefeatScene` | `DefeatScene` |
21. 
22. Register scenes in `src/main.ts`. The Phaser 4 configuration uses FIT scaling,
23. centered pixel art, and zoom 6.
24. 
25. ## Imports and class shape
26. 
27. ```typescript
28. import * as Phaser from "phaser";
29. 
30. export class ExampleScene extends Phaser.Scene {
31.   constructor() {
32.     super({ key: "ExampleScene" });
33.   }
34. 
35.   init(data: ExampleSceneData): void {
36.     // Store and normalize scene input.
37.   }
38. 
39.   create(): void {
40.     // Build display objects, input, audio, and scene-owned helpers.
41.   }
42. }
43. ```
44. 
45. Use explicit types and return values. Store Phaser objects that need later
46. updates or cleanup as class properties.
47. 
48. ## Semantic input
49. 
50. `src/systems/input.ts` owns stable action/context contracts and pure state.
51. `src/managers/input.ts` is the single browser adapter for keyboard, pointer,
52. standard gamepads, and touch. Scenes must use the shared actions or existing
53. keyboard/pointer behavior reached by that adapter rather than adding independent
54. gamepad/mobile mappings. The adapter clears held input on scene changes, blur,
55. visibility loss, disconnect, and shutdown.
56. 
57. Touch controls use safe-area-aware responsive DOM buttons outside the canvas.
58. Held D-pad directions use pointer capture; discrete buttons use click pulses so
59. scene transitions cannot strand a press. Standard gamepads use left-stick/D-pad
60. navigation and a visible right-stick cursor, clicked by pressing the stick, for
61. pointer-first surfaces.
62. 
63. Feature-gated semantic actions use `src/systems/featureDiscovery.ts`. Dynamic
64. menus and tabs rebuild from filtered entries, clamp selection, remove hidden
65. hit areas, and update procedural touch controls. Untaught shortcuts stay inert,
66. while always-safe cancel, Tips, Settings, Inventory, Map, Equipment, and
67. save/title paths remain available.
68. 
69. `CodexScene` keeps category, filter, sort, and search controls pointer-first so
70. touch and the gamepad cursor share the keyboard surface. Search uses
71. `openMobileTextInput()`. `CodexDiscoveryManager` owns non-interactive,
72. scene-local notices and must be cleared on shutdown; it never changes input
73. context or delays scene transitions.
74. 
75. `AchievementOverlayManager` owns the accessible Achievements/profile surface and
76. presentation-only title selection. `AchievementNotificationManager` reads
77. persisted pending IDs but displays them only in safe Overworld states; scene
78. shutdown clears visuals without acknowledging an interrupted notice. Both must
79. support keyboard, pointer, touch-menu access, gamepad cursor, text scaling,
80. high contrast, and reduced motion.
81. 
82. `GatheringManager` owns the in-place fishing/mining/foraging overlay, input,
83. timers, pointer controls, status record, and cleanup. Overworld resumes pending
84. gathering before World Events, blocks movement and other interactions while it
85. is open, and routes guarded rare finds through Battle with resolution hooks.
86. 
87. ## Shared state flow
88. 
89. State-bearing transitions use `createSharedSceneState()` and preserve:
90. 
91. ```typescript
92. interface SharedSceneState {
93.   player: PlayerState;
94.   defeatedBosses: Set<string>;
95.   codex: CodexData;
96.   timeStep: number;
97.   weatherState: WeatherState;
98.   savedSpecialNpcs: SavedSpecialNpc[];
99. }
100. ```
101. 
102. Scene-specific additions:
103. 
104. - Battle: `encounter: MonsterEncounter`, `biome`, optional accessor-backed
105.   `partyCombatants`, optional runtime-only `battleHooks`; Battle may return
106.   transient `questUpdates` to Overworld after victory
107. - Shop: `townName`, optional item IDs, city context, discount, and optional
108.   stable `shopSkillCheckId`
109. - Overworld: fields are optional only because Boot can create or load the
110.   initial state
111. - Cutscene: full shared state, stable `CutsceneId`, replay mode, return scene,
112.   and optional runtime-only `questUpdates`
113. - Ending: full shared state plus the campaign-epilogue `CutsceneId`
114. - Defeat: full shared state plus encounter name/type and an exact runtime-only
115.   `PartyDefeatResult`
116. 
117. When a scene contract changes, update every `scene.start()` caller in the same
118. change.
119. 
120. `player.party` is persistent nested state and travels automatically with
121. `player`. Battle may additionally receive runtime-only accessor-backed
122. `partyCombatants`; never serialize those wrappers.
123. 
124. ## Transition pattern
125. 
126. ```typescript
127. this.sceneTransitions.startWithFade(() => {
128.   this.scene.start("OverworldScene", {
129.     player: this.player,
130.     defeatedBosses: this.defeatedBosses,
131.     codex: this.codex,
132.     timeStep: this.timeStep,
133.     weatherState: this.weatherState,
134.     savedSpecialNpcs: this.savedSpecialNpcs,
135.   });
136. }, {
137.   duration: 500,
138.   label: "return to overworld",
139. });
140. ```
141. 
142. Do not serialize `Set<string>` during scene transitions. Conversion to arrays
143. belongs in the save system.
144. 
145. `SceneTransitionManager` is the single owner of camera fades and queued scene
146. handoffs. Instantiate it once per scene, call `prepare()` at the start of
147. `create()`, and use its guarded start/restart methods instead of direct
148. fade-plus-timer pairs. Fade-complete events are primary; the duration-plus-grace
149. watchdog only recovers missing events. The manager must remove completed
150. listeners/timers, restore the outgoing camera before queueing the next scene,
151. and suppress duplicate handoffs during Phaser's one-update queue delay.
152. It resolves fade durations through the shared reduced-motion accessor and uses
153. an immediate guarded handoff when motion is disabled.
154. 
155. Call `installSceneAccessibility(this)` in every scene `create()`. The adapter
156. applies live text scale and high contrast, exposes preference state on the
157. canvas for browser assertions, and suppresses residual tweens in reduced-motion
158. mode. New scene animations must also branch through
159. `isReducedMotionEnabled()` or `getMotionDuration()`.
160. 
161. Use `ActorAnimationDirector` for reusable actor poses and cleanup. Specialized
162. battle/world directors register sprites by stable actor ID, use explicit
163. `ActorTextureFamily` frame keys with fallback textures, and expose deterministic
164. debug state for browser synchronization. Kill owned tweens/timers on shutdown;
165. never wait for actor animation before an authoritative fade-complete handoff.
166. 
167. Overworld restarts use one shared payload that includes a fresh
168. `savedSpecialNpcs` snapshot. Block movement and other state-changing actions
169. while a handoff is pending.
170. 
171. Queue and save cutscene IDs before presentation. `CutsceneScene` and
172. `EndingScene` mark an ID seen and dequeue it only after completion or skip, then
173. chain the next pending ID. Reload resumes the first pending scene. Chronicle
174. replay never mutates progression. A skipped pre-boss scene still executes its
175. completion metadata and starts the selected fight. Add an input grace period
176. when a dialogue keypress can cross a scene boundary.
177. 
178. ## Procedural assets
179. 
180. `BootScene.preload()` calls texture generation from
181. `src/renderers/textures.ts`. Add new procedural texture generation there and
182. invoke it through the existing aggregate generator. Do not load image, sprite,
183. or audio files.
184. 
185. Player-specific runtime textures are the exception to Boot-time aggregation:
186. resolve their typed descriptor from live `PlayerState` with `heroVisuals.ts`,
187. acquire them through `heroTextures.ts`, and release the lease only after the
188. owning sprite/container is destroyed or has switched textures. This keeps
189. cutscene recovery and Chronicle replay current without generic-frame flashes or
190. texture leaks.
191. 
192. ## Scene-owned subsystems
193. 
194. Overworld delegates to renderers and managers. Instantiate these in `init()` so
195. a restarted scene receives fresh helpers, then load persisted data into them:
196. 
197. - `FogOfWar`
198. - `EncounterSystem`
199. - `MapRenderer`
200. - `CityRenderer`
201. - `PlayerRenderer`
202. - `HUDRenderer`
203. - `OverlayManager`
204. - NPC and dialogue managers
205. - `QuestJournalManager`
206. - `QuestFlowManager`
207. - `ChronicleManager`
208. - `SkillCheckManager`
209. - `DebugCommandSystem`
210. - `CompanionFollowerManager`
211. - `PartyOverlayManager`
212. 
213. Battle delegates companion manual/gambit turn UI to `BattlePartyManager` and
214. companion presentation to `BattlePartyRenderer`. Destroy their transient
215. containers on scene exit/restart.
216. 
217. `BattleBackdropRenderer` owns all scene-sized environment containers, actor
218. shadows, split rear/front weather, lightning timers, inspection labels, and
219. cleanup. Use `BATTLE_DEPTH` for backdrop, actor, presentation, weather, and UI
220. objects; opaque sky geometry must remain below celestial bodies and scenery.
221. 
222. Before replacing `FogOfWar` or `EncounterSystem`, preserve their debug toggle
223. state so Battle, Shop, and Codex round trips do not re-enable fog or encounters.
224. 
225. ## UI layout
226. 
227. - Use `src/systems/layout.ts` for pure measured stacks, grids, wrapping,
228.   pagination, safe-area clamping, and focus restoration.
229. - Use `src/managers/layout.ts` for actual scaled Phaser bounds, text-stack
230.   reflow, hit-area synchronization, and debug/test overlap audits.
231. - Register modal containers with `createOverlayContainer()` and their final
232.   content viewport. Give interactive rows stable `layoutId` values.
233. - Filter hidden or disabled entries before layout; variable-length menus must
234.   not retain fixed indexes, blank rows, or invisible hit targets.
235. - Keep action buttons visibly disabled outside the player turn.
236. - Destroy or replace transient menus before opening another.
237. - For scrollable text, bound what is rendered to the visible area.
238. 
239. Phaser 4 geometry masks do not reliably clip the Battle log in this project.
240. The Battle scene renders only messages that fit and changes the message offset
241. on mouse-wheel input.
242. 
243. ## Battle lifecycle
244. 
245. - Reinitialize phase, menus, turn flags, discoveries, and monster effects in
246.   `init()`.
247. - Build fresh per-monster combatants, sprites, text, status arrays, defend
248.   flags, discovery state, and initiative order in `init()`.
249. - Create the hero through `createHeroCombatant()` so HP/effects stay backed by
250.   PlayerState; companion wrappers use the same `PartyCombatant` contract.
251. - Process player and each monster's statuses at that actor's turn boundaries.
252. - Dispatch initiative by `combatantId`. Companion turns route through
253.   `onCompanionTurn`, which receives all actors plus execution/log adapters and
254.   must call `completeTurn()`.
255. - Companion turn context also supplies weather penalty, synergy defense, and
256.   elemental-discovery adapters for `executeValidatedBattleAction()`.
257. - Companion hooks use the pure `battleActions.ts` planner for gambit matching,
258.   target validation, and action dispatch rather than scene-local rules.
259. - BattleScene's hero action flags are backed by the same
260.   `BattleActionEconomyState`; reset it at the start of each hero turn.
261. - Skip defeated initiative entries and keep Player Defend active until the
262.   next player turn.
263. - Target mode supports pointer selection, arrows/WASD cycling, Enter/Space
264.   confirmation, Esc cancellation, gamepad selection/confirmation, and touch.
265. - Battle action buttons expose a non-color `▶` selection marker for keyboard and
266.   gamepad focus before targeting.
267. - Keep bonus-action abilities and the first item use on the player turn.
268. - Validate actions before consuming MP, items, or the turn.
269. - Clear player and every monster's combat effects before leaving Battle.
270. - Guard every Battle exit through `SceneTransitionManager`. Start Overworld or
271.   `DefeatScene` from `FADE_OUT_COMPLETE` or the delayed recovery watchdog, and
272.   restore the outgoing camera before Phaser queues the handoff.
273. - Report victory, defeat, or flee once through `onBattleResolved`; reward
274.   adjustment happens before XP/gold are granted.
275. - On defeat, apply the party penalty once, autosave the recovered state, pass
276.   the exact receipt to `DefeatScene`, and never recalculate it there. Random and
277.   boss encounters use the same recovery mechanics.
278. - After group victory, record every defeated combatant ID for quest counters
279.   without deduplicating repeated monster types, then pass transient updates to
280.   Overworld for notification and autosave.

7. # World and Map System
8. 
9. ## Module layout
10. 
11. - `src/data/map.ts`: hub, shared helpers, encounter rates, and re-exports
12. - `src/data/mapTypes.ts`: terrain enum, interfaces, and dimensions
13. - `src/data/chunks.ts`: 10x9 overworld chunk grid
14. - `src/data/cities.ts`: city layouts, districts, shops, and gates
15. - `src/data/dungeons.ts`: dungeon floors and stairs
16. - `src/data/traps.ts`: trap definitions and persistent trap types
17. - `src/data/quests.ts`: progression-gated city and dungeon entrances
18. - `src/systems/movement.ts`: grid, city-gate, and dungeon-stair movement
19. - `src/systems/traps.ts`: seeded placement, checks, effects, and rewards
20. - `src/managers/dungeonTraps.ts`: dungeon trap scene orchestration
21. - `src/systems/quests.ts`: quest entrance-block checks
22. - `src/managers/fogOfWar.ts`: exploration-key generation and reveal state
23. - `src/managers/skillChecks.ts`: terrain events, hidden treasure, and chest
24.   checks
25. - `src/data/worldEvents.ts`: immutable World Event definitions and eligibility
26. - `src/systems/worldEvents.ts`: seeded selection, outcomes, persistence repair
27. - `src/managers/worldEvents.ts`: accessible choices and Battle handoff
28. - `src/renderers/map.ts`: terrain and weather rendering
29. - `src/renderers/city.ts`: city NPC, animal, and district rendering
30. 
31. ## Dimensions
32. 
33. - World: 10x9 chunks
34. - Chunk/interior: 20x15 tiles
35. - Tile size: 32x32 pixels
36. - Map arrays are always `[y][x]`
37. 
38. ## Terrain
39. 
40. `Terrain` currently spans IDs 0-43. Important navigation additions:
41. 
42. - `CityGate = 41`
43. - `DungeonStairs = 42`
44. - `DungeonBoss = 43`
45. 
46. Use `isWalkable()` and `ENCOUNTER_RATES` for behavior. Stairs, gates, and boss
47. tiles are walkable and do not produce random encounters.
48. Apply day/night, weather, and mount modifiers through
49. `getEffectiveEncounterRate()`; the effective random-encounter chance is capped
50. at 15%.
51. 
52. ## Overworld
53. 
54. Use:
55. 
56. ```typescript
57. getChunk(chunkX, chunkY);
58. getTerrainAt(chunkX, chunkY, tileX, tileY);
59. getTownBiome(chunkX, chunkY, tileX, tileY);
60. ```
61. 
62. Chunk names drive biome music, weather probabilities, and presentation. New
63. names must retain a recognized biome prefix.
64. 
65. ## Nautical world
66. 
67. `src/data/nautical.ts` overlays four stable landmasses, five sea zones, ports,
68. merchant routes, islands, boats, and sea pools on the unchanged 10x9 chunk
69. grid. `src/systems/nauticalState.ts` owns schema-v16 normalization;
70. `nautical.ts` owns sailing/routes/hazards/encounters; `nauticalOwnership.ts`
71. owns acquisition, upgrades, cosmetics, and repairs. Only a serviceable active
72. boat may traverse `Terrain.Water`; walking still uses `isWalkable()`.
73. 
74. Sea fog keys use `s:zoneId,chunkX,chunkY,x,y`. Merchant routes are atomic and
75. available before boat ownership. Disembarkation validates canonical walkability
76. and rejects towns, dungeons, bosses, chests, events, and other blocked landing
77. tiles. Sea encounter rates always pass through `getEffectiveEncounterRate()`.
78. 
79. ## Random World Events
80. 
81. World Events run only on ordinary overworld movement after the move and
82. day/weather updates complete. Chunk transitions, city/dungeon entrances, traps,
83. NPC/special interactions, and queued cutscenes have priority. Within the
84. post-movement chain the order is World Event, minor treasure, exploration skill
85. check, then random encounter.
86. 
87. Event probability uses its own data-driven 8% cap and never changes
88. `getEffectiveEncounterRate()` or its 15% cap. Eligibility may include terrain,
89. chunk-name area prefixes, day/night period, weather, level, quest/boss state,
90. prior outcomes, repeat limits, and cooldowns. Persist the selected pending event
91. before presentation so reload cannot reroll it.
92. 
93. ## Quest-gated entrances
94. 
95. Quest barriers guard true interaction chokepoints rather than isolated
96. overworld edge tiles, which are easy to walk around. Use
97. `getBlockedQuestEntrance()` for city/dungeon actions and
98. `getBlockedQuestEntranceAt()` for rendering the matching barricade tile.
99. 
100. Sandport and the Heartlands Crypt remain reachable. Canyonwatch opens during
101. `sunRoad` after `sandportPass`, Ashfall opens at `ashenWatch`, and the Volcanic
102. Forge opens at `lastForge`. Add data-integrity tests that entrance coordinates
103. still match their city or dungeon definition.
104. 
105. Premature northern, marsh, and ashen travel uses persisted soft danger rules.
106. Pass their encounter multiplier through `getEffectiveEncounterRate()` and add
107. their effective-level offset only when choosing random encounters.
108. 
109. ## Exploration skill checks
110. 
111. Terrain-driven Wisdom discoveries and Dexterity hazards are defined in
112. `src/data/skillChecks.ts`. Select them through the shared skill-check helpers;
113. do not hardcode event rolls in the scene.
114. 
115. ## Codex exploration
116. 
117. City and dungeon entry emit idempotent Codex location signals. Readable records
118. reuse stable non-walkable temple/statue coordinates defined in
119. `src/data/codexKnowledge.ts`; interaction is adjacent and presentation-only.
120. Do not add lore flags to map terrain or use Codex state for access decisions.
121. 
122. ## Multi-chunk cities
123. 
124. `CityData.mapData`, `spawnX`, `spawnY`, and `shops` represent chunk 0. The
125. optional `chunks` array stores additional districts starting at logical index
126. 1. Never index that array using the logical city chunk index.
127. 
128. Use:
129. 
130. ```typescript
131. getCityChunkCount(city);
132. getCityChunk(city, chunkIndex);
133. getCityChunkMap(city, chunkIndex);
134. getCityChunkSpawn(city, chunkIndex);
135. getCityChunkShops(city, chunkIndex);
136. getCityChunkShopNearby(city, chunkIndex, x, y);
137. getCityConnectionAt(city, chunkIndex, x, y);
138. ```
139. 
140. `CityData.connections` maps a source gate tile to a destination district and
141. tile. Movement through a connection updates `player.position.cityChunkIndex`,
142. `x`, and `y`.
143. 
144. When adding a district:
145. 
146. 1. Add a 20x15 `CityChunk`.
147. 2. Place reachable `Terrain.CityGate` tiles.
148. 3. Add both travel directions when the gate should be bidirectional.
149. 4. Add district shops to that chunk.
150. 5. Test map dimensions, walkability, connection destinations, and reachability.
151. 
152. ## Multi-level dungeons
153. 
154. Level 0 remains in `DungeonData.mapData`; `levels[0]` is logical level 1.
155. Use:
156. 
157. ```typescript
158. getDungeonTotalLevels(dungeon);
159. getDungeonLevelMap(dungeon, level);
160. getDungeonLevelSpawn(dungeon, level);
161. getDungeonConnectionAt(dungeon, level, x, y);
162. getDungeonBoss(dungeonId);
163. ```
164. 
165. `DungeonData.connections` contains explicit source and destination levels and
166. tiles. Model ascent and descent as separate connections. The deepest floor
167. contains `Terrain.DungeonBoss` and a unique `bossId`.
168. 
169. Dungeon encounters should pass the dungeon ID so the correct exclusive pool is
170. used.
171. Random encounters may be replaced by a level- and environment-valid
172. `MonsterEncounter`; dungeon bosses and explicit debug spawns remain solo.
173. 
174. ## Dungeon traps
175. 
176. Each `DungeonData` has a `trapProfile` with allowed types, a thematic type,
177. per-level count, and difficulty modifier. Generate layouts only through:
178. 
179. ```typescript
180. generateDungeonTraps(dungeon, level, player.progression.trapSeed);
181. ```
182. 
183. Layouts are immutable metadata overlays. They use stable IDs, prioritize tiles
184. adjacent to dungeon chests, and exclude the level spawn plus exit/stair/boss
185. approaches. The same seed recreates the same layout; trap resolution lives in
186. authoritative `player.progression.trapStates` entries.
187. 
188. Run one detection check when a trap first becomes adjacent or the player tries
189. to enter its tile. `detected` traps block entry and expose a Space-to-disarm
190. prompt. `missed` traps trigger on entry and must not be rerolled. Hidden-floor
191. drops use `getDungeonLevelSpawn()` on the next level.
192. 
193. ## Chests
194. 
195. Dungeon chest locations may include `dungeonLevel`. Resolve the level map
196. before reading a chest tile. Opened chest IDs remain globally unique and are
197. stored in player progression.
198. 
199. `ChestData` may also define `lockDc`/`trapDamage` and
200. `secretDc`/`secretGold`. Lock failures can deal nonlethal damage, while secret
201. checks can grant bonus gold. Persist results with stable chest-derived check
202. IDs so a fixed check cannot be rerolled.
203. 
204. ## Fog of war
205. 
206. Always generate keys through `FogOfWar.exploredKey()`.
207. 
208. | Location | Key |
209. | --- | --- |
210. | Overworld | `chunkX,chunkY,x,y` |
211. | Dungeon level 0 | `d:dungeonId,x,y` |
212. | Dungeon level N | `d:dungeonId,level,x,y` |
213. | City chunk 0 | `c:cityId,x,y` |
214. | City chunk N | `c:cityId,chunkIndex,x,y` |
215. 
216. The level-zero and chunk-zero formats intentionally preserve existing saves.
217. `revealEntireWorld()` must cover every dungeon level and city district.
218. 
219. Achievement exploration progress reads `discoveredCities`, persistent
220. skill-check/trap state, and `FogOfWar.exploredKey()` values. It may derive unique
221. overworld chunks or dungeon completion, but it must never write map access,
222. terrain, fog, city, dungeon, or quest state.
223. 
224. ## Player position
225. 
226. ```typescript
227. interface PlayerPosition {
228.   x: number;
229.   y: number;
230.   chunkX: number;
231.   chunkY: number;
232.   inDungeon: boolean;
233.   dungeonId: string;
234.   dungeonLevel: number;
235.   inCity: boolean;
236.   cityId: string;
237.   cityChunkIndex: number;
238. }
239. ```
240. 
241. Dungeon and city flags are mutually exclusive. Save loading validates IDs,
242. clamps levels/chunks, repairs invalid tiles to the correct spawn, and falls back
243. to the Willowdale overworld start when necessary.
244. 
245. ## Gathering nodes
246. 
247. Fishing uses adjacent Water/River terrain, mining uses adjacent blocked rock,
248. mountain, volcanic, or dungeon-wall terrain, and foraging uses current or
249. adjacent forest/vegetation terrain. Resolve current maps through chunk/city/
250. dungeon helpers, keep approaches walkable and clear of transition/chest/boss
251. tiles, and derive stable node IDs from context, sublevel, discipline, and target
252. tile. Gathering is an explicit interaction and blocks movement-step events,
253. skill checks, traps, and encounters while active.
254. 
255. ## Crafting acquisition
256. 
257. Minor overworld treasures derive a canonical common material deterministically
258. from their stable location key while preserving gold. Selected chests use typed
259. bonus material rewards without replacing their primary item. Shops and monster
260. drop tables may expose balanced canonical materials, but epic materials stay
261. rare and no campaign-critical route may require them.
262. 
263. ## Common pitfalls
264. 
265. - Indexing maps as `[x][y]`
266. - Treating `city.chunks[0]` as logical chunk 0
267. - Using `dungeon.levels[level]` directly
268. - Adding only one direction of a reversible connection
269. - Reusing fog keys across floors or districts
270. - Looking up only generic dungeon monsters and omitting exclusive pools/bosses
271. - Hardcoding walkability or encounter behavior
272. - Mutating map terrain to store trap state
273. - Rerolling layouts or detection checks after reload
274.

2. name: dnd-mechanics
3. description: Implement 2D&D's D&D 5E-inspired stats, combat, elements, and statuses correctly
4. license: MIT

6. 
7. # D&D-Inspired Mechanics
8. 
9. 2D&D adapts D&D 5E concepts to a single-player JRPG. Follow the implemented
10. rules in `src/systems/` when they intentionally differ from tabletop rules.
11. 
12. ## Ability scores
13. 
14. The six scores are Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom,
15. and Charisma.
16. 
17. ```typescript
18. abilityModifier(score) === Math.floor((score - 10) / 2);
19. ```
20. 
21. Character creation supports:
22. 
23. - 27-point buy
24. - Base score range 8-15
25. - Costs: 8/0, 9/1, 10/2, 11/3, 12/4, 13/5, 14/7, 15/9
26. - Optional 4d6-drop-lowest generation
27. - Class boosts applied after base scores
28. 
29. ## Classes
30. 
31. | Class | Boosts | Primary stat |
32. | --- | --- | --- |
33. | Knight | STR +2, CON +1 | STR |
34. | Ranger | DEX +2, WIS +1 | DEX |
35. | Wizard | INT +2, WIS +1 | INT |
36. | Sorcerer | CHA +2, CON +1 | CHA |
37. | Rogue | DEX +2, CHA +1 | DEX |
38. | Paladin | STR +1, CHA +2 | CHA |
39. | Warlock | CHA +2, INT +1 | CHA |
40. | Cleric | WIS +2, CON +1 | WIS |
41. | Druid | WIS +2, CON +1 | WIS |
42. | Barbarian | STR +2, CON +1 | STR |
43. | Monk | DEX +2, WIS +1 | DEX |
44. | Bard | CHA +2, DEX +1 | CHA |
45. 
46. The class `primaryStat` is used for attack/to-hit calculations where the
47. specific action does not override the stat.
48. 
49. ## Non-combat ability checks
50. 
51. Use `src/systems/skillChecks.ts` for exploration and dialogue checks:
52. 
53. ```typescript
54. total = naturalD20 + abilityModifier(player.stats[ability]);
55. success = total >= dc;
56. ```
57. 
58. - Dexterity: lockpicking, trap disarming, and escaping hazards
59. - Wisdom: hidden loot, paths, passages, and exploration events
60. - Charisma: Persuade/Bluff NPC outcomes and shop negotiation
61. - Natural 1 and 20 do not automatically fail or succeed on these checks
62. - Fixed outcomes are one-time and persist in
63.   `player.progression.skillChecks`
64. - Exploration damage is nonlethal and cannot reduce the player below 1 HP
65. 
66. Gathering minigames do not apply unrelated ability modifiers silently. Related
67. future talents or tools may modify explicit data-driven difficulty, but fishing,
68. mining, and foraging use readable input patterns with identical reduced-motion
69. thresholds and rewards.
70. 
71. ## Core combat
72. 
73. - Attack rolls use d20 + ability modifier + proficiency/bonuses.
74. - Natural 20 automatically hits and is critical.
75. - Natural 1 automatically misses.
76. - Initiative uses d20 + Dexterity modifier.
77. - Spells consume MP rather than spell slots.
78. - Armor Class comes from base AC, Dexterity, equipment, talents, active
79.   statuses, and temporary defense bonuses.
80. - Group initiative rolls once for the player and once per monster, then
81.   interleaves all actors by total using stable combatant IDs. Companion actors
82.   use the same initiative contract.
83. - Melee must clear the front row before attacking the back row. Once exposed,
84.   back-row melee targets impose -2 to the attack roll; ranged attacks and
85.   spells ignore this formation penalty.
86. 
87. Use the combat functions in `src/systems/combat.ts`; do not reimplement formulas
88. inside scenes.
89. 
90. ## Advantage and disadvantage
91. 
92. Roll two d20s and select the higher/lower natural roll before adding modifiers.
93. Natural 1 and natural 20 behavior must be based on the selected die, not the
94. first die rolled.
95. 
96. Poisoned, Frightened, and Prone currently impose attack disadvantage. Magic
97. Missile is auto-hit and bypasses attack-roll disadvantage.
98. AoE spells pay MP once and share one attack/damage roll, while elemental
99. resistance, weakness, and immunity resolve independently per target.
100. Healing target scopes are explicit: self, one ally, all allies, or the whole
101. party. A single-ally action falls back to self when no ally is present.
102. 
103. ## Elements
104. 
105. `src/data/elements.ts` defines:
106. 
107. - Fire
108. - Ice
109. - Lightning
110. - Poison
111. - Necrotic
112. - Radiant
113. - Thunder
114. - Force
115. - Psychic
116. 
117. Elemental profile order is:
118. 
119. 1. Immunity: damage becomes 0.
120. 2. Weakness: damage is doubled.
121. 3. Resistance: damage is floored after halving.
122. 4. Otherwise unchanged.
123. 
124. Status damage modifiers are applied before the elemental modifier. Record
125. observed non-neutral interactions in the Codex.
126. 
127. Monster `affinity` is presentation and roster metadata using the same canonical
128. nine-element enum. Damage still resolves only through ability/spell elements and
129. the target's `elementalProfile`; family data must not create a parallel damage
130. rule.
131. 
132. ## Status effects
133. 
134. `src/systems/statusEffects.ts` is the single source of truth.
135. 
136. Debuffs:
137. 
138. - Poisoned: turn damage and attack disadvantage
139. - Burning: fire damage each turn
140. - Frozen: reduced accuracy and AC
141. - Paralyzed: skipped turns and reduced AC
142. - Stunned: one skipped turn
143. - Frightened: attack disadvantage and reduced damage
144. - Slowed: reduced accuracy and damage
145. - Prone: attack disadvantage and reduced AC
146. - Asleep: skipped turns until save/expiration
147. - Confused: reduced accuracy
148. 
149. Buffs:
150. 
151. - Enraged: increased damage and reduced AC
152. - Hasted: increased accuracy and AC
153. - Inspired: increased accuracy and damage
154. - Raging: increased damage
155. - Sneak Stance: increased AC
156. 
157. Lifecycle for each actor:
158. 
159. 1. Start turn: resolve tick damage, allowed saving throws, and skip-turn state.
160. 2. Perform or skip the action.
161. 3. End turn: decrement duration and expire effects.
162. 
163. A one-turn stun therefore skips exactly one actor turn. Cure items remove only
164. matching effects. Combat effects are cleared when leaving Battle.
165. 
166. ## Dungeon trap checks
167. 
168. - Detection and disarming use d20 + the configured Dexterity or Intelligence
169.   modifier through `resolveSkillCheck()` / `rollSkillCheck()` with a validated
170.   situational modifier.
171. - Trap Kits, Natural Explorer, Cunning Action, and persistent Adventurer
172.   guidance add their defined bonuses; Danger Sense detects automatically.
173. - Failed detection persists in authoritative `trapStates`, so checks cannot be
174.   farmed by stepping away or reloading.
175. - Successful disarming awards XP through `awardXP()`.
176. - Trigger damage and MP loss apply immediately and cannot reduce HP below 1.
177.   Trap-applied statuses seed the next battle and then follow the existing
178.   combat-turn lifecycle.
179. - Alarm traps replace the normal encounter roll with a forced dungeon
180.   encounter. Hidden floors use the next level's validated spawn.
181. 
182. ## Action economy
183. 
184. - Attack, spell, defend, flee, and normal abilities consume the action.
185. - Bonus-action abilities do not schedule the monster turn.
186. - The first item use in a turn is a bonus action.
187. - Invalid spell/ability/item choices must not consume MP, inventory, or turn
188.   state.
189. - Every party actor owns an immutable one-action/one-bonus-action economy.
190.   Manual and gambit-controlled companion actions use the same validator and
191.   executor as the hero-compatible battle contracts.
192. - Animation is presentation-only: resolve and consume the validated action
193.   exactly once before emitting actor/target feedback. Tween completion must
194.   never apply damage, spend resources, or advance action economy.
195. 
196. ## Companion progression
197. 
198. - Recruits match the hero level deterministically, then gain XP and levels
199.   independently.
200. - Living party members receive battle XP. A KO member receives no victory XP
201.   and resets to the current-level XP floor (`0` at level 1).
202. - Full defeat occurs only when every active party actor is KO. Apply the
203.   current-level XP floors and 30% carried-gold loss once, restore defeated
204.   actors to half HP/MP, clear battle effects, and recover at the last town.
205.   Return the exact before/after receipt for `DefeatScene`; boss and random
206.   encounters use identical mechanics. Inn rest still fully restores and
207.   processes pending levels for all recruited companions.
208. - Party-wide heal/buff spells consume MP once and resolve each valid target.
209. - Gambit and UI actions pass through `validateBattleAction()` before execution;
210.   validated plans bind stable actor/target IDs and declare action or bonus
211.   action cost.
212. - `BattleActionEconomyState` tracks one action and one bonus action per actor;
213.   consuming a bonus action leaves the main action available for lower-ranked
214.   gambits.
215. - Generic outbound actors execute validated plans through the same d20, AC,
216.   element, status, healing, MP, inventory, and defend paths as the hero.
217. - Battle consumables use item-declared target scopes. Ally items fall back to
218.   self when solo, self-only items remain self, and inventory ownership stays
219.   separate from the effect target.
220. - Inventory sorting and filtering are presentation-only. Preserve canonical
221.   ownership order, exact equipment links, and equipped/key/mount transfer
222.   restrictions while resolving actions through original inventory indexes.
223. - Crafting is deterministic rather than a d20 check. Validate every ingredient,
224.   batch, gold/station requirement, and output before mutation; equipment upgrades
225.   intentionally replace exact equipped links while unrelated equipped, key,
226.   mount, and quest items remain protected.
227. - Flee DC is 10 for one monster and increases by 2 for each additional living
228.   monster. Boss encounters cannot be fled.
229. 
230. ## Leveling
231. 
232. - Proficiency increases at levels 5, 9, 13, and 17.
233. - Ability score improvements occur at levels 4, 8, 12, 16, and 19.
234. - Pending level gains are applied by the existing rest/level processing logic.
235. - Class hit dice and unlock tables are defined in `src/systems/classes.ts`.
236. 
237. ## Alignment and reputation
238. 
239. - Alignment uses two bounded axes: Law/Chaos and Good/Evil, both from -100 to
240.   100. Scores at +25 or higher use the positive label; scores at -25 or lower
241.   use the negative label; the middle band is Neutral.
242. - New heroes begin at `lawChaos: -50`, `goodEvil: 0`, exactly Chaotic Neutral.
243. - Reputation is independent per canonical town and faction. Tiers are Hostile,
244.   Wary, Neutral, Friendly, Trusted, and Exalted.
245. - Apply shifts only through `applySocialMutation()` with a stable source ID.
246.   Routine combat and movement never change alignment or reputation.
247. - Reputation shop adjustments are additive with Charisma negotiation and clamp
248.   to a 25% surcharge or 35% discount.
249. 
250. ## Achievement-specific mechanics
251. 
252. - A one-hit defeat requires one damaging action to take an enemy from its full
253.   maximum HP to zero; prior chip or status damage disqualifies it.
254. - The no-defeat campaign achievement uses explicit schema-v13 party-defeat
255.   history. Older saves have unknown history and cannot receive it by inference.
256. - Achievements and equipped cosmetic titles never modify ability scores, AC,
257.   attacks, damage, rewards, or action economy.
258. 
259. ## Testing

+# 2D&D
+
+[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mbianchidev/2dnd)](https://github.com/mbianchidev/2dnd/releases/latest)
+[![Pull request checks](https://github.com/mbianchidev/2dnd/actions/workflows/pr.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/mbianchidev/2dnd/actions/workflows/pr.yml)

+[![License: AGPL-3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
+
+**A browser JRPG with Dragon Quest-style exploration and D&D 5E-inspired
+combat.** Build a hero, recruit a party, cross a 90-chunk world, and complete
+the seven-chapter Twelvefold Covenant campaign.
+
+**[Play 2D&D now](https://mbianchidev.github.io/2dnd/)**  
+Current release: **v1.0.0**
+
+2D&D runs entirely in the browser. Its pixel-art textures are generated at
+runtime, its music and sound effects are synthesized with the Web Audio API,
+and campaign saves stay in your browser's local storage.
+
+## Highlights
+
+- **Create your hero:** choose from 12 classes, use 27-point buy or
+  4d6-drop-lowest stats, customize appearance, level to 20, and collect
+  equipment, talents, spells, abilities, and mounts.
+- **Complete a full campaign:** follow the Twelvefold Covenant through 12
+  mainland cities, three keystone dungeons, data-driven cutscenes, boss
+  encounters, an epilogue, and post-game continuation.
+- **Build a party:** recruit the Guardian, Scout, and Mystic; manage their
+  equipment and inventories; control them manually or automate turns with
+  ranked gambits.
+- **Fight tactical battles:** face groups of up to four enemies with initiative,
+  formations, ally and enemy targeting, nine elements, status effects, healing,
+  items, bosses, and full-party defeat recovery.
+- **Explore a changing world:** travel through connected city districts,
+  multi-level dungeons, seeded traps, fog of war, weather, day and night,
+  non-combat skill checks, World Events, and optional danger zones.
+- **Discover more than monsters:** expand the Codex with lore, make alignment
+  and reputation choices, earn achievements and cosmetic titles, and replay
+  unlocked story scenes in the Chronicle.
+- **Gather, craft, and sail:** fish, mine, forage, craft deterministic recipes
+  and equipment upgrades, use merchant routes, earn a boat, explore Tidehaven,
+  and challenge the Deepwake Kraken.
+- **Play your way:** use keyboard, pointer, touch, or a standard gamepad.
+  Accessibility settings include 100%/125%/150% text, high contrast, reduced
+  motion, adjustable audio, cutscene advance options, and adaptive prompts.
+
+See the [gameplay guide](docs/gameplay.md) for controls, progression, and player
+guidance.
+
+## Browser and save support
+
+2D&D is designed for current desktop and mobile browsers. Release CI validates
+the game in Chromium; other current evergreen browsers are expected to work but
+are not part of the automated release gate. There is no desktop installer.
+
+Campaign saves, accessibility/audio settings, and inventory-view preferences
+are stored locally in the current browser profile. Saves do not automatically
+sync between browsers, devices, private windows, or cleared site data. The game
+has no account system, analytics, or server-side save service.
+
+## Run locally
+
+The CI baseline is Node.js 24 with npm.
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/mbianchidev/2dnd.git
+cd 2dnd
+npm ci
+npm run dev
+```
+
+Open `http://localhost:3000`.
+
+```bash
+npm run typecheck      # Strict TypeScript validation
+npm test               # Full Vitest suite
+npm run test:browser   # Full Playwright/Chromium suite
+npm run build          # Type-check and build dist/
+```
+
+Install Chromium once before the browser suite with
+`npm run test:browser:install`.
+
+## Documentation
+
+| Guide | Contents |
+| --- | --- |
+| [Documentation index](docs/README.md) | Complete documentation map |
+| [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) | Installation, local hosting, saves, troubleshooting |
+| [Gameplay](docs/gameplay.md) | Controls, campaign, combat, exploration, accessibility |
+| [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | Scene flow, domain ownership, input, transitions, procedural assets |
+| [Development](docs/development.md) | Conventions, feature placement, debug tools, dependencies |
+| [Testing](docs/testing.md) | Vitest, Playwright, layout/accessibility checks, CI gates |
+| [Save system](docs/save-system.md) | Schema v17, migration, recovery, persistence rules |
+| [Release](docs/release.md) | GitHub Pages and release checklist |
+| [Companions and gambits](docs/companions.md) | Party state, recruitment, AI, combat integration |
+| [Inventory presentation](docs/inventory.md) | Ownership-safe sorting, filtering, controls, transfers |
+
+## Contributing
+
+Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), the
+[development guide](docs/development.md), and the
+[testing guide](docs/testing.md) before changing the game. Open an
+[issue](https://github.com/mbianchidev/2dnd/issues) for bugs or proposals and
+submit changes through a pull request.
+
+## License

+# Gameplay guide
+
+[Documentation index](README.md) | [Getting started](getting-started.md)
+
+## The adventure
+
+2D&D is a browser JRPG built around exploration, party growth, turn-based
+combat, and a complete campaign. Create a hero from 12 classes, travel through
+the 90-chunk world, recruit up to three active companions, restore three
+keystones, and return to Elowen to complete the Twelvefold Covenant.
+
+The campaign includes seven chapters, 12 mainland cities, connected districts,
+three campaign dungeons, story and boss cutscenes, optional objectives, an
+epilogue, credits, Chronicle replay, and post-game continuation. Tidehaven and
+the Deepwake Kraken form an optional island and sea-navigation arc.
+
+## Core controls
+
+Feature-specific shortcuts become available only after the corresponding
+system has been discovered. The Escape menu remains the reliable entry point.
+
+| Keyboard | Action |
+| --- | --- |
+| `WASD` / arrows | Move, navigate menus, cycle valid Battle targets |
+| `Space` / `Enter` | Confirm, interact, or disarm a detected adjacent trap |
+| `Esc` | Cancel, close the active overlay, or skip an active cutscene |
+| `F1` | Open Tips |
+| `M` | Open the map |
+| `E` | Open equipment |
+| `Q` | Open the quest journal after discovery |
+| `P` | Open party management after recruiting a companion |
+| `C` | Open the Codex after discovery |
+| `Y` | Open Achievements after the first natural unlock |
+| `K` | Open Gathering after discovering a discipline |
+| `V` | Open Crafting after learning a non-starting recipe |
+| `T` | Mount or dismount after acquiring a mount |
+
+Pointer and touch users can select visible buttons directly. Touch layouts use
+safe-area-aware movement and action controls. Standard gamepads use the left
+stick or D-pad for movement/navigation, `A` to confirm, `B` to cancel, `X` to
+interact, Menu/`Y` for the menu, View for Tips, bumpers for targets/pages, and
+triggers for Battle-log scrolling. The right stick moves a visible cursor;
+press the stick to click pointer-first controls.
+
+Mappings are stable rather than user-remappable. Settings can control touch
+visibility, handedness, and automatic or fixed prompt sources.
+
+## Character creation and progression
+
+Character creation follows:
+
+**Name -> Class -> Stats -> Appearance -> Adventure**
+
+- Choose Knight, Ranger, Wizard, Sorcerer, Rogue, Paladin, Warlock, Cleric,
+  Druid, Barbarian, Monk, or Bard.
+- Spend 27 points on base scores from 8 to 15, or use 4d6-drop-lowest random
+  generation.
+- Class boosts apply after base stats.
+- Level progression reaches 20 with class actions, spells, talents, equipment,
+  hit-point growth, proficiency increases, and ability-score improvements.
+
+## Party, inventory, and gambits
+
+Guardian, Scout, and Mystic join through their own quests. Recruited companions
+have independent levels, stats, HP/MP, equipment, inventories, abilities,
+spells, status effects, and control settings. Up to three active companions
+follow the hero without blocking movement or triggering world interactions.
+
+Party members can be controlled manually or by up to 12 ranked gambit rules.
+Gambits evaluate a fresh turn snapshot, skip invalid rules without spending
+resources, and can use one bonus action plus one main action.
+
+See [Companions and gambits](companions.md) and
+[Inventory presentation](inventory.md).
+
+## Combat
+
+Battles use d20 attacks, Dexterity initiative, natural 1/20 attack outcomes,
+critical hits, Armor Class, defending, fleeing, spells, abilities, items, and
+boss actions. Encounters contain one to four independent enemies with stable
+initiative identities and front/back formations.
+
+Nine elements are supported: Fire, Ice, Lightning, Poison, Necrotic, Radiant,
+Thunder, Force, and Psychic. Immunities prevent damage, weaknesses double it,
+and resistances halve it. Observed interactions become Codex knowledge.
+
+Combat statuses include Poisoned, Burning, Frozen, Paralyzed, Stunned,
+Frightened, Slowed, Prone, Asleep, Confused, Enraged, Hasted, Inspired, Raging,
+and Sneak Stance. Effects resolve on actor turn boundaries and are cleared when
+Battle ends.
+
+A full party wipe applies one recovery result, autosaves it, reports exact gold
+and XP losses, clears Battle effects, and returns the party to the last town at
+half HP/MP.
+
+## Exploration
+
+The world contains 90 legacy-compatible chunks, 13 cities including optional
+Tidehaven, and four multi-level dungeons including Tideglass Grotto. Exploration
+includes:
+
+- connected city districts, shops, inns, banks, stables, and fast travel
+- day/night lighting, six weather types, biome encounters, and fog of war
+- hidden paths, treasure, dialogue, negotiation, and non-combat d20 checks
+- seeded dungeon traps with persistent detected, missed, disarmed, or triggered
+  outcomes
+- data-driven World Events with choices, skill checks, rewards, special
+  battles, cooldowns, and reload recovery
+- alignment, town/faction reputation, optional reactions, and bounded shop
+  modifiers
+- monster and world-lore Codex entries, achievements, cosmetic titles, and the
+  Chronicle
+
+## Gathering, crafting, and sailing
+
+Fishing, mining, and foraging use deterministic location-based nodes and
+discipline-specific minigames. The selected pattern and reward are saved before
+play, so reloading cannot reroll the outcome. Rare guarded finds use the normal
+Battle flow.
+
+Crafting consumes canonical materials in atomic transactions. Recipes cover
+healing, cures, travel supplies, trap tools, equipment upgrades, and elemental
+gear. Upgrades preserve exact equipment ownership links.
+
+Merchant routes work before boat ownership. Later, the Tideglass Charter grants
+a Reed Skiff for free sailing, hazards, sea encounters, open-water fishing,
+boat upgrades, island discovery, Tideglass Grotto, and the optional Kraken.
+
+## Tutorial, discovery, and accessibility
+
+New campaigns open a five-step tutorial after the opening cutscene queue.
+Completing or skipping it prevents automatic replay; it can still be replayed
+from Tips.
+
+Menus, shortcuts, tabs, prompts, touch actions, and advanced Tips reveal from
+authoritative gameplay evidence. Safety-critical surfaces such as Inventory,
+Map, Equipment, Tips, Settings, save, and title controls remain available.
+
+Accessibility and presentation settings include:
+
+- 100%, 125%, and 150% text
+- high contrast and non-color-only state cues
+- reduced motion with immediate completion semantics
+- master, music, SFX, dialog, and mute controls
+- manual or automatic cutscene advance
+- touch visibility, handedness, and prompt-source controls
+
+Settings are stored separately from campaign progress. See
+[Getting started](getting-started.md#local-save-data) for storage details.

+# Architecture
+
+[Documentation index](README.md) | [Development](development.md) |
+[Save system](save-system.md)
