1. # Development guide
2. 
3. [Documentation index](README.md) | [Architecture](architecture.md) |
4. [Testing](testing.md) | [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)
5. 
6. ## Working principles
7. 
8. - Use strict TypeScript with explicit parameter and return types.
9. - Do not use `any`; validate `unknown` with guards.
10. - Prefer interfaces for object shapes and type aliases for unions/intersections.
11. - Use `import type` for type-only imports.
12. - Keep immutable content in `src/data/` and reusable Phaser-free logic in
13.   `src/systems/`.
14. - Keep scene orchestration in `src/scenes/`, stateful helpers in
15.   `src/managers/`, and procedural presentation in `src/renderers/`.
16. - Reuse existing helpers before adding a parallel implementation.
17. - Use `debugLog()` and debug-panel APIs; do not add production `console.log`.
18. - Do not mutate shared monster, item, map, city, dungeon, quest, or recipe data.
19. - No external image/audio assets and no gameplay network calls.
20. - When a source file exceeds 1,000 lines, consider extracting a focused module
21.   before adding another responsibility.
22. 
23. ## Where to add common work
24. 
25. | Change | Primary files |
26. | --- | --- |
27. | Combat formula or status | `src/systems/combat.ts`, `statusEffects.ts`, `groupCombat.ts` |
28. | Player/companion action | `src/systems/battleActions.ts`, data action definition, focused tests |
29. | Monster or encounter | `src/data/monsters.ts`, `monsterVariants.ts`, `nightMonsters.ts`, `seaMonsters.ts`, `monsterGroups.ts` |
30. | Quest | `src/data/quests.ts`, `src/systems/quests.ts`, quest tests |
31. | Cutscene | focused `src/data/cutscene*.ts`, `src/systems/cutscenes.ts`, cutscene tests |
32. | World/city/dungeon | `src/data/map*.ts`, `chunks.ts`, `cities.ts`, `dungeons.ts`, map helpers |
33. | Sea navigation | `src/data/nautical.ts`, `src/systems/nautical*.ts`, `src/data/islands.ts` |
34. | Gathering/crafting | matching `src/data/`, `src/systems/`, and `src/managers/` modules |
35. | Save field | owning interface/default, normalization module, `src/systems/save.ts`, migration tests |
36. | Input/control | `src/systems/input.ts`, `src/managers/input.ts`; never a scene-local gamepad map |
37. | UI layout | `src/systems/layout.ts`, `src/managers/layout.ts`, owning manager/renderer |
38. | Texture | focused renderer aggregated by `src/renderers/textures.ts` |
39. | Audio | `src/systems/audio.ts` and typed domain profile helpers |
40. 
41. Read the matching `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md` before implementing domain work.
42. 
43. ## Dependency and build workflow
44. 
45. CI uses Node.js 24.
46. 
47. ```bash
48. npm ci
49. npm audit
50. npm run typecheck
51. npm test
52. npm run test:browser
53. npm run build
54. ```
55. 
56. Do not add a new linter, test runner, formatter, or build system for a one-off
57. task. Change dependencies only when the feature requires it, keep
58. `package-lock.json` synchronized, and verify the audit result.
59. 
60. ## Debug tools
61. 
62. Debug mode is available only on local hosts through the checkbox above the
63. canvas. Shared commands live in `src/systems/debug.ts`; scene-specific adapters
64. provide validated callbacks.
65. 
66. Useful command families include:
67. 
68. ```text
69. /spawn
70. /battleview
71. /backdrop
72. /quest
73. /near
74. /cutsceneview
75. /companion
76. /event
77. /alignment
78. /reputation
79. /achievement
80. /feature
81. /gather
82. /craft
83. ```
84. 
85. Use debug commands to create deterministic browser states, then synchronize
86. Playwright on debug-state transitions or stable layout IDs instead of arbitrary
87. sleep durations and coordinates.
88. 
89. ## Utility scripts
90. 
91. Repository utilities belong in `hacks/` and must be documented in
92. `hacks/instructions.md`. Temporary scripts must be removed when the task is
93. finished. Do not add planning or summary Markdown files to the repository.
94. 
95. The permanent `hacks/run-browser-tests.mjs` wrapper allocates a fresh local port
96. for the Playwright suite.
97. 
98. ## Documentation ownership
99. 
100. Update documentation in the same change when behavior, commands, architecture,
101. versions, controls, or persistent data change:
102. 
103. - public discovery and quick start: root `README.md`
104. - detailed topic guidance: `docs/`
105. - agent workflow and ownership routing: root `AGENTS.md`
106. - repository-wide constraints: `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
107. - domain implementation rules: `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md`
108. 
109. Do not describe issue proposals or open pull requests as shipped behavior.
110. Verify claims against current `main`.
111.

1. # Testing
2. 
3. [Documentation index](README.md) | [Development](development.md) |
4. [Release](release.md)
5. 
6. 2D&D uses Vitest for deterministic logic/contracts and Playwright for
7. high-value browser integration. Documentation-only changes still run the release
8. gate before delivery because stale commands, paths, and integration assumptions
9. can break the public workflow.
10. 
11. ## Commands
12. 
13. ```bash
14. npm run typecheck
15. npm test
16. npm run test:browser:install
17. npm run test:browser
18. npm run build
19. ```
20. 
21. `npm run build` already performs a TypeScript check before Vite builds `dist/`,
22. but the standalone typecheck remains a separate release gate and gives faster
23. diagnostics.
24. 
25. ## Vitest responsibilities
26. 
27. Tests in `tests/*.test.ts` own Phaser-free behavior:
28. 
29. - combat, elements, statuses, target scopes, action economy, rewards
30. - player and companion progression, gambits, inventories, transfers
31. - quests, cutscene triggers/queues, Codex, events, social state, achievements
32. - gathering, crafting, nautical state, world/map/trap/fog helpers
33. - save round trips, migrations, corruption repair, and cross-field validation
34. - semantic input mappings, context priority, repeats, cleanup, and suppression
35. - pure layout, wrapping, pagination, safe-area, and focus math
36. - transition contracts with mocked camera/time adapters
37. 
38. Random mechanics must accept deterministic values or seeded state. Test the
39. authoritative helper rather than reproducing formulas in assertions.
40. 
41. ## Playwright responsibilities
42. 
43. The `e2e/*.spec.ts` suites own real browser behavior:
44. 
45. - new game through campaign completion, ending, post-game, and reload
46. - interrupted opening/ending/cutscene recovery and corrupt-save fallback
47. - random and boss defeat recovery
48. - tutorial, Tips, Codex, inventory, achievements, events, gathering, crafting,
49.   nautical, feature discovery, and accessibility
50. - keyboard, pointer, touch, gamepad, mobile text entry, and active-source prompts
51. - actor animation, current-player cutscene visuals, Battle backdrops, cleanup,
52.   screenshots, and page/console errors
53. - layout audits at supported text scales and representative desktop/mobile
54.   viewports
55. 
56. `playwright.config.ts` defaults to `/2dnd/`, uses one worker, and starts Vite on
57. a strict port. `hacks/run-browser-tests.mjs` allocates a free port and disables
58. server reuse so tests cannot silently attach to stale code.
59. 
60. To exercise the local root base explicitly:
61. 
62. ```bash
63. PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_PATH=/ npm run test:browser
64. ```
65. 
66. ## Stable browser synchronization
67. 
68. - Prefer stable debug-state transitions, layout IDs, and semantic actions.
69. - Hold frame-polled Phaser keys across animation frames; instantaneous presses
70.   can be missed.

44.

48.

50. - selected pending outcomes that must survive reload without rerolling
51. - non-reconstructable counters and bounded histories

104. | Browser test on stale server/root path | `npm run test:browser`; fresh strict port and `/2dnd/` default |
105. | Docs copied from an issue or branch | Verify current `main`, source constants, package manifest, and merged PR |
106. | Parallel features merged in arbitrary order | Identify shared files, choose dependency order, rebase after prerequisite, preserve both contracts |

108. | Growing scenes/overlays | Extract focused system, manager, renderer, or data module |

1. # Companions and Gambits
2. 
3. [Documentation index](README.md) | [Gameplay](gameplay.md) |
4. [Architecture](architecture.md)
5. 
6. ## Party model
7. 
8. The persistent party was introduced in schema v6 and lives at `player.party` in
9. the current schema v17:
10. 
11. - `companions`: unique recruited `CompanionState` records
12. - `activeCompanionIds`: up to three recruited IDs in battle/follower order
13. 
14. The hero remains the owner of gold, bank balance, world position, mounts, and
15. world progression. Each companion owns independent XP, level, HP/MP, stats,
16. spells, abilities, talents, inventory, equipment, active effects, dialogue
17. cursor, control mode, and gambits.
18. 
19. The three stable companion IDs are:
20. 
21. | ID | Role | Class |
22. | --- | --- | --- |
23. | `guardian` | Defensive frontline | Paladin |
24. | `scout` | Mobile ranged damage | Ranger |
25. | `mystic` | Healing and party support | Cleric |
26. 
27. New recruits match the hero's current level using deterministic historical HP
28. and MP growth. Later XP and level-ups are independent.
29. 
30. ## Recruitment
31. 
32. Recruitment uses the canonical quest system:
33. 
34. - `recruitGuardian`
35. - `recruitScout`
36. - `recruitMystic`
37. 
38. Each quest has stable `meet*`, `*Trial`, and `*Oath` stage IDs and emits one
39. completion action:
40. 
41. ```text
42. companion.recruit.guardian
43. companion.recruit.scout
44. companion.recruit.mystic
45. ```
46. 
47. `replayQuestCompletionActions(..., "recruitCompanion")` runs after load,
48. Overworld initialization, NPC quest changes, and debug quest mutations.
49. `recruitCompanion()` is idempotent, so reloads, rewinds, and repeated debug
50. completion cannot duplicate a companion or starter inventory. Debug quest and
51. companion commands refresh the live follower sprites immediately.
52. 
53. ## Party management
54. 
55. Press `P` during exploration to open the party overlay.
56. 
57. The overlay supports:
58. 
59. - active/reserve membership and active order
60. - manual or gambit combat control
61. - member stats, HP/MP/XP, and equipment
62. - independent inventories and item transfer
63. - targeted consumables and healing outside combat
64. - pending companion stat allocation
65. - ranked gambit editing
66. 
67. The Items page uses immutable sorted and filtered views, full-text search,
68. procedural item visuals, and stable keyboard/pointer selection for large bags.
69. Its sort, filter, and search preferences are stored separately from actor
70. ownership. See [`inventory.md`](inventory.md) for controls and selector rules.
71. 
72. Key items, mounts, and equipped items cannot be transferred. Gold remains with
73. the hero; shop purchases and battle drops enter the hero bag and can then be
74. transferred.
75. 
76. ## Gambit rules
77. 
78. Each companion can store up to 12 enabled or disabled rules. Rank 1 has highest
79. priority.
80. 
81. The structured rule format is:
82. 
83. ```text
84. if [subject] has/is [condition] do [action] on [target]
85. ```
86. 
87. Supported subjects include self, hero, any party member, a specific companion,
88. and any enemy. Conditions cover HP/MP values or percentages, statuses,
89. alive/KO state, and ability-score comparisons. Actions cover attack, defend,
90. known spells, known abilities, and owned items. Targets include the matched
91. subject, named party members, lowest/highest HP allies or enemies, and
92. automatic area targets.
93. 
94. At the start of a gambit-controlled turn:
95. 
96. 1. Status start-of-turn processing resolves.
97. 2. Rules are evaluated by ascending rank against a fresh battle snapshot.
98. 3. Invalid targets, missing items, insufficient MP, consumed action slots, and
99.    inapplicable heals/buffs fall through without mutation.
100. 4. A valid bonus action may execute first.
101. 5. Lower-ranked rules continue until one main action executes.
102. 6. If no rule executes, the companion attacks; if no enemy is valid, it
103.    defends.
104. 
105. Manual companion turns and gambits both use `validateBattleAction()` and
106. `executeValidatedBattleAction()`.
107. 
108. ## Battle, KO, and rewards
109. 
110. Every conscious party member rolls initiative. Monsters select only living
111. party actors. Battle ends in defeat only when the whole active party is KO.
112. 
113. Living members receive victory XP. A member knocked out during the battle
114. receives no victory XP and loses progress earned toward the next level, down to
115. the current-level XP floor. A partially victorious KO member remains at 0 HP
116. until an inn.
117. 
118. On a full wipe:
119. 
120. - every active member receives the KO XP penalty
121. - the existing 30% hero-gold penalty applies once
122. - the party returns to the last town
123. - active members recover half HP/MP
124. - Battle effects are cleared and the recovered state is autosaved
125. - `DefeatScene` shows every defeated member, exact gold/XP losses, and the
126.   recovery location before continuing; boss and random encounters share this
127.   path
128. 
129. Inn rest revives and fully restores every recruited companion and processes
130. their pending level-ups.
131. 
132. ## Followers and world integration
133. 
134. Active conscious companions follow the hero using prior valid hero tiles. They
135. do not block movement or independently trigger traps, encounters, gates, or
136. world interactions. Pointer interaction talks directly to a follower; Space
137. uses companion dialogue only after higher-priority world interactions.
138. 
139. Dungeon movement preserves `DungeonTrapManager` ordering:
140. 
141. ```text
142. trap move/arrival handling -> exploration event -> random encounter
143. ```
144. 
145. Companions travel inside the existing `player` scene payload, so Battle, Shop,
146. Codex, fast travel, alarm encounters, and scene restarts preserve one party
147. state without a parallel transition field.
148. 
149. ## Debug commands
150. 
151. ```text
152. /companion list
153. /companion recruit <guardian|scout|mystic|all>
154. /companion mode <id> <manual|gambit>
155. /companion heal
156. /companion gambits <id>
157. ```
158. 
159. The debug MP hotkey is `O`; `P` is reserved for party management.
160.

1. # Inventory presentation
2. 
3. [Documentation index](README.md) | [Gameplay](gameplay.md) |
4. [Companions and gambits](companions.md)
5. 
6. ## Ownership and presentation
7. 
8. Hero and companion item ownership remains in each actor's canonical
9. `inventory` array. Equipment fields continue to reference the exact owned item
10. objects. Inventory presentation is derived by `src/systems/inventory.ts` and
11. must never sort, splice, or replace the canonical array.
12. 
13. Presentation preferences use the separate `2dnd_inventory_prefs` local-storage
14. key:
15. 
16. - sort: type, value, rarity, recent acquisition, or name
17. - filter: all, equipment, consumables, quest items, or crafting items
18. - search text
19. 
20. Recent acquisition is the reverse of canonical append order, so it requires no
21. ownership metadata or save-schema migration. Future crafting items use the
22. `crafting` item type and already participate in selectors and generated visuals.
23. 
24. ## Party and menu access
25. 
26. Press `P` to open party management, then select **Items**. The `Esc` menu also
27. opens the same Party & Inventory surface directly. `T` remains reserved for
28. mount control.
29. 
30. Inventory controls:
31. 
32. | Input | Action |
33. | --- | --- |
34. | `Up` / `Down` | Move the stable item selection |
35. | `Page Up` / `Page Down` | Move one visible page |
36. | `Home` / `End` | Select the first or last result |
37. | `Enter` | Use, equip, or inspect the selected item |
38. | `X` | Transfer the selected item to the current target |
39. | `R` | Cycle sort mode |
40. | `F` | Cycle filter |
41. | `/` | Focus search; `Enter` finishes typing |
42. | `Tab` | Cycle the party target |
43. 
44. Every action is also available through pointer buttons. The manager exposes
45. semantic inventory actions so future gamepad and mobile controls can invoke the
46. same behavior without emulating keyboard keys.
47. 
48. ## Restrictions
49. 
50. - Equipped items cannot transfer.
51. - Key items and mounts remain hero-owned.
52. - Equipment actions target the owning actor.
53. - Consumables use the existing validated target and consumption rules.
54. - Sorting, filtering, and search return entries with their original inventory
55.   indexes, so duplicate items and equipment links remain stable.
56. 
57. Generated item visuals are drawn procedurally from item type and rarity; no
58. external assets are used.
59.

## Project

2D&D is a browser JRPG combining Dragon Quest-style exploration with
D&D 5E-inspired combat. It has turn-based battles, point-buy characters,
procedural graphics/audio, weather, day/night, a 90-chunk world, connected city
districts, multi-level dungeons, procedural traps, non-combat skill checks,
quest-recruited companions, ranked gambits, elemental interactions, status
effects, boss fights, and a replayable campaign epilogue with post-game
continuation, plus deterministic fishing, mining, and foraging minigames.

1. # Development guide
2. 
3. [Documentation index](README.md) | [Architecture](architecture.md) |
4. [Testing](testing.md) | [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)
5. 
6. ## Working principles
7. 
8. - Use strict TypeScript with explicit parameter and return types.
9. - Do not use `any`; validate `unknown` with guards.
10. - Prefer interfaces for object shapes and type aliases for unions/intersections.
11. - Use `import type` for type-only imports.
12. - Keep immutable content in `src/data/` and reusable Phaser-free logic in
13.   `src/systems/`.
14. - Keep scene orchestration in `src/scenes/`, stateful helpers in
15.   `src/managers/`, and procedural presentation in `src/renderers/`.
16. - Reuse existing helpers before adding a parallel implementation.
17. - Use `debugLog()` and debug-panel APIs; do not add production `console.log`.
18. - Do not mutate shared monster, item, map, city, dungeon, quest, or recipe data.
19. - No external image/audio assets and no gameplay network calls.
20. - When a source file exceeds 1,000 lines, consider extracting a focused module
21.   before adding another responsibility.
22. 
23. ## Where to add common work
24. 
25. | Change | Primary files |
26. | --- | --- |
27. | Combat formula or status | `src/systems/combat.ts`, `statusEffects.ts`, `groupCombat.ts` |
28. | Player/companion action | `src/systems/battleActions.ts`, data action definition, focused tests |
29. | Monster or encounter | `src/data/monsters.ts`, `monsterVariants.ts`, `nightMonsters.ts`, `seaMonsters.ts`, `monsterGroups.ts` |
30. | Quest | `src/data/quests.ts`, `src/systems/quests.ts`, quest tests |
31. | Cutscene | focused `src/data/cutscene*.ts`, `src/systems/cutscenes.ts`, cutscene tests |
32. | World/city/dungeon | `src/data/map*.ts`, `chunks.ts`, `cities.ts`, `dungeons.ts`, map helpers |
33. | Sea navigation | `src/data/nautical.ts`, `src/systems/nautical*.ts`, `src/data/islands.ts` |
34. | Gathering/crafting | matching `src/data/`, `src/systems/`, and `src/managers/` modules |
35. | Save field | owning interface/default, normalization module, `src/systems/save.ts`, migration tests |
36. | Input/control | `src/systems/input.ts`, `src/managers/input.ts`; never a scene-local gamepad map |
37. | UI layout | `src/systems/layout.ts`, `src/managers/layout.ts`, owning manager/renderer |
38. | Texture | focused renderer aggregated by `src/renderers/textures.ts` |
39. | Audio | `src/systems/audio.ts` and typed domain profile helpers |
40. 
41. Read the matching `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md` before implementing domain work.
42. 
43. ## Dependency and build workflow
44. 
45. CI uses Node.js 24.
46. 
47. ```bash
48. npm ci
49. npm audit
50. npm run typecheck
51. npm test
52. npm run test:browser
53. npm run build
54. ```
55. 
56. Do not add a new linter, test runner, formatter, or build system for a one-off
57. task. Change dependencies only when the feature requires it, keep
58. `package-lock.json` synchronized, and verify the audit result.
59. 
60. ## Debug tools
61. 
62. Debug mode is available only on local hosts through the checkbox above the
63. canvas. Shared commands live in `src/systems/debug.ts`; scene-specific adapters
64. provide validated callbacks.
65. 
66. Useful command families include:
67. 
68. ```text
69. /spawn
70. /battleview
71. /backdrop
72. /quest
73. /near
74. /cutsceneview
75. /companion
76. /event
77. /alignment
78. /reputation
79. /achievement
80. /feature
81. /gather
82. /craft
83. ```
84. 
85. Use debug commands to create deterministic browser states, then synchronize
86. Playwright on debug-state transitions or stable layout IDs instead of arbitrary
87. sleep durations and coordinates.
88. 
89. ## Utility scripts
90. 
91. Repository utilities belong in `hacks/` and must be documented in
92. `hacks/instructions.md`. Temporary scripts must be removed when the task is
93. finished. Do not add planning or summary Markdown files to the repository.
94. 
95. The permanent `hacks/run-browser-tests.mjs` wrapper allocates a fresh local port
96. for the Playwright suite.
97. 
98. ## Documentation ownership
99. 
100. Update documentation in the same change when behavior, commands, architecture,
101. versions, controls, or persistent data change:
102. 
103. - public discovery and quick start: root `README.md`
104. - detailed topic guidance: `docs/`
105. - agent workflow and ownership routing: root `AGENTS.md`
106. - repository-wide constraints: `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
107. - domain implementation rules: `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md`
108. 
109. Do not describe issue proposals or open pull requests as shipped behavior.
110. Verify claims against current `main`.
111.

1. # Testing
2. 
3. [Documentation index](README.md) | [Development](development.md) |
4. [Release](release.md)
5. 
6. 2D&D uses Vitest for deterministic logic/contracts and Playwright for
7. high-value browser integration. Documentation-only changes still run the release
8. gate before delivery because stale commands, paths, and integration assumptions
9. can break the public workflow.
10. 
11. ## Commands
12. 
13. ```bash
14. npm run typecheck
15. npm test
16. npm run test:browser:install
17. npm run test:browser
18. npm run build
19. ```
20. 
21. `npm run build` already performs a TypeScript check before Vite builds `dist/`,
22. but the standalone typecheck remains a separate release gate and gives faster
23. diagnostics.
24. 
25. ## Vitest responsibilities
26. 
27. Tests in `tests/*.test.ts` own Phaser-free behavior:
28. 
29. - combat, elements, statuses, target scopes, action economy, rewards
30. - player and companion progression, gambits, inventories, transfers
31. - quests, cutscene triggers/queues, Codex, events, social state, achievements
32. - gathering, crafting, nautical state, world/map/trap/fog helpers
33. - save round trips, migrations, corruption repair, and cross-field validation
34. - semantic input mappings, context priority, repeats, cleanup, and suppression
35. - pure layout, wrapping, pagination, safe-area, and focus math
36. - transition contracts with mocked camera/time adapters
37. 
38. Random mechanics must accept deterministic values or seeded state. Test the
39. authoritative helper rather than reproducing formulas in assertions.
40. 
41. ## Playwright responsibilities
42. 
43. The `e2e/*.spec.ts` suites own real browser behavior:
44. 
45. - new game through campaign completion, ending, post-game, and reload
46. - interrupted opening/ending/cutscene recovery and corrupt-save fallback
47. - random and boss defeat recovery
48. - tutorial, Tips, Codex, inventory, achievements, events, gathering, crafting,
49.   nautical, feature discovery, and accessibility
50. - keyboard, pointer, touch, gamepad, mobile text entry, and active-source prompts
51. - actor animation, current-player cutscene visuals, Battle backdrops, cleanup,
52.   screenshots, and page/console errors
53. - layout audits at supported text scales and representative desktop/mobile
54.   viewports
55. 
56. `playwright.config.ts` defaults to `/2dnd/`, uses one worker, and starts Vite on
57. a strict port. `hacks/run-browser-tests.mjs` allocates a free port and disables
58. server reuse so tests cannot silently attach to stale code.
59. 
60. To exercise the local root base explicitly:
61. 
62. ```bash
63. PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_PATH=/ npm run test:browser
64. ```
65. 
66. ## Stable browser synchronization
67. 
68. - Prefer stable debug-state transitions, layout IDs, and semantic actions.
69. - Hold frame-polled Phaser keys across animation frames; instantaneous presses
70.   can be missed.
71. - Do not target fixed canvas coordinates when a registered layout ID exists.
72. - Do not depend on fixed sleeps alone.
73. - Wait for fade-complete-driven scene state, not the nominal fade duration.
74. - Keep screenshot tolerance focused on genuine cross-platform raster variance;
75.   functional assertions remain primary.
76. - Treat page errors, unexpected console errors, overlaps, and clipping as test
77.   failures.
78. 
79. The local `#layout-report` and canvas
80. `data-layout-overlap-count`/`data-layout-clipping-count` attributes are
81. debug/test surfaces. Registered groups should report zero unintended
82. intersections and zero visible-content clipping.
83. 
84. ## Targeted validation
85. 
86. During implementation, run the smallest related Vitest files first. Run focused
87. Playwright specs for changed UI/scene flows. Before a pull request, run:
88. 
89. 1. `npm ci`
90. 2. `npm audit`
91. 3. `npm run typecheck`
92. 4. `npm test`
93. 5. `npm run test:browser`
94. 6. `npm run build`
95. 7. `git diff --check`
96. 
97. If a dependency install reports vulnerabilities, resolve or explicitly account
98. for them before release.
99. 
100. ## CI
101. 
102. `.github/workflows/pr.yml` runs Node 24, `npm ci`, typecheck, full Vitest,
103. Chromium installation, full Playwright, and the production build for pull
104. requests to `main`.
105. 
106. `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` analyzes Actions and JavaScript/TypeScript.
107. GitHub Pages deployment separately runs `npm ci`, Vitest, and the production
108. build from `main`.
109.

 # 2D&D
 
-A browser-based JRPG that combines Dragon Quest-style exploration with
-Dungeons & Dragons 5E-inspired combat. The game runs entirely in the browser:
-graphics are procedurally generated, audio is synthesized with the Web Audio
-API, and saves use `localStorage`.
-
-## Features
-
-### Character creation and progression
-
-- 12 classes: Knight, Ranger, Wizard, Sorcerer, Rogue, Paladin, Warlock,
-  Cleric, Druid, Barbarian, Monk, and Bard
-- D&D 5E point buy: 27 points, base scores from 8 to 15
-- Optional 4d6-drop-lowest random stat generation
-- Class ability boosts, class-specific primary stats, spells, martial
-  abilities, talents, equipment, shields, mounts, and banking
-- Leveling to 20 with hit-die HP growth, proficiency bonuses, and ability score
-  improvements
-- Three quest-recruited companions (Guardian, Scout, Mystic) with independent
-  levels, stats, HP/MP, spells, abilities, equipment, inventories, and ASI
-  progression
-- Hero plus three active companions, reserve/active ordering, item transfers,
-  party-wide inn recovery, and persistent manual or gambit control
-- Large hero and companion inventories support immutable sorting by type,
-  value, rarity, recent acquisition, or name; category filters, search,
-  generated item visuals, and stable keyboard, pointer, gamepad, and touch
-  selection
-- Ranked 12-rule gambits use structured subjects, conditions, actions, and
-  targets; invalid rules safely fall through without consuming resources
-
-### Combat
-
-- Turn-based d20 combat with initiative, natural 1/20 outcomes, critical hits,
-  defending, fleeing, off-hand attacks, spells, abilities, consumables, and
-  boss abilities
-- Balanced encounters with 1-4 monsters, individual initiative turns,
-  front/back formations, semantic keyboard, pointer, gamepad, or touch target
-  selection, and group
-  synergies such as Pack Tactics, Shield Wall, War Cry, healer support, and
-  elemental combos
-- Party battles use stable combatant IDs, explicit party/enemy allegiance,
-  individual initiative, ally/enemy target scopes, living-party monster target
-  selection, manual companion turns, automated gambits, and shared result hooks
-- `battleActions.ts` provides a Phaser-free gambit pipeline to enumerate living
-  actors, bind matched and item-declared ally/self targets, validate
-  MP/inventory/action economy, freeze an action plan, consume one action plus
-  one bonus action per actor, and dispatch one attack, defend, spell, ability,
-  or item action
-- Generic `BattleActionSource` and `executeValidatedBattleAction()` reuse the
-  game's d20, AC, elements, statuses, MP, inventory, healing, and defend rules
-  for player or future companion actors
-- Battle consumables use item-declared target scopes: ally items fall back to
-  self when solo, self-only items remain self, and the acting actor consumes
-  the item while HP, MP, or cures apply to the selected target
-- Single-target, row-targeted, random-two, and all-enemy spell targeting; AoE
-  spells pay MP and roll damage once, then resolve each monster independently
-- Single/all-party healing, Mass Haste, and Inspiring Chorus apply one shared
-  roll/cost across the resolved party targets
-- Nine damage elements: Fire, Ice, Lightning, Poison, Necrotic, Radiant,
-  Thunder, Force, and Psychic
-- Monster weaknesses deal double damage, resistances halve damage, and
-  immunities prevent damage
-- Elemental interactions are discovered through combat and recorded per
-  monster in the Codex
-- Every monster belongs to one of 14 typed families with a stable base/variant
-  relationship, weighted encounter eligibility, and a family-specific
-  procedural silhouette. Palette variants keep distinct abilities, drops,
-  elemental profiles, and difficulty, while bosses use richer family forms.
-- The typed Codex preserves monster defeat, AC, elemental, drop, family, and
-  completion discovery while adding locations, items, characters, factions,
-  and history from canonical campaign data.
-- Knowledge unlocks are idempotent and source-driven through city/dungeon
-  exploration, quest stages/completions, cutscenes, item acquisition, named NPC
-  dialogue, and readable statues or temple records. Lore never controls quests,
-  rewards, companions, gates, or outcomes.
-- Category filters, search, canonical/name/source sorting, discovered grouping,
-  source hints, and non-blocking discovery notices support keyboard, pointer,
-  touch, gamepad cursor, 150% text, high contrast, and reduced motion.
-- 15 status effects shared by players and monsters:
-  Poisoned, Burning, Frozen, Paralyzed, Stunned, Frightened, Slowed, Prone,
-  Asleep, Confused, Enraged, Hasted, Inspired, Raging, and Sneak Stance
-- Start-of-turn damage and saving throws, skipped turns, attack disadvantage,
-  accuracy/AC/damage modifiers, duration expiration, and cure items
-- Combat effects are cleared when Battle ends because their durations use the
-  combat turn clock
-- Full-party defeat opens a dedicated procedural result sequence for random and
-  boss encounters, lists every defeated actor, reports the exact gold and XP
-  losses, autosaves the recovered state, and continues from the last town with
-  half HP/MP and no battle effects or overlapping weather ambience
-- Stable-ID battle presentation animates hero, companion, monster, and boss
-  idle, attack, cast, ability, item, defend, damage, victory, faint, and flee
-  states after mechanics resolve, without changing action economy or outcomes
-
-### Non-combat skill checks
-
-- D20 ability checks use the player's Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or
-  Charisma modifier;
-  natural 1 and 20 are not automatic outcomes outside attack rolls
-- Charisma supports persistent Persuade/Bluff NPC outcomes and one-attempt shop
-  negotiations with 10% or 20% discounts
-- Wisdom uncovers hidden trails, dungeon passages, secret chest compartments,
-  and better rewards from overworld treasure
-- Dexterity avoids exploration hazards and resolves locked or trapped chests;
-  failed hazards can cost HP but cannot defeat the player outside combat
-- Fixed checks use stable save IDs, while repeatable terrain events remain
-  data-driven by environment and terrain
-
-### World exploration
-
-- A 10x9 world grid containing 90 chunks, each 20x15 tiles
-- Four named landmasses—Frostcrown, Verdant Covenant, Ember March, and
-  Southreach—assigned over the unchanged 90 legacy chunk identities, with five
-  navigable sea zones and compatible overworld fog coordinates
-- Discoverable ports and merchant routes support paid passage before boat
-  ownership; The Tideglass Charter grants a Reed Skiff and unlocks free sailing,
-  safe contextual embark/disembark, boat condition, upgrades, and cosmetics
-- Tidehaven island adds a two-district town, harbor shops and inn, sea materials,
-  a multi-level trapped grotto, and the optional Deepwake Kraken boss
-- Sailing alone enables capped sea encounters, day/night sea pools, weather
-  hazards, open-sea fishing, synthesized wake/audio, and procedural boat art
-- Distinct terrain, biome encounter tables, night encounters, weather,
-  day/night lighting, fog of war, treasure, NPCs, animals, and special NPCs
-- Random encounter modifiers stack but the effective chance is capped at 15%;
-  group encounters begin at level 2 and use level budgets and biome filters
-- Seeded, data-driven World Events add shrines, ambushes, travelers, discoveries,
-  weather hazards, and supply finds. Eligibility uses terrain, area, day/night,
-  weather, level, quest state, prior outcomes, repeat limits, and cooldowns.
-- Event choices reuse normal skill checks, quest/reward helpers, Codex
-  `worldEvent` signals, and the standard Battle pipeline. Pending choices and
-  special combats recover after reload without rerolling or duplicating rewards.
-- The Chronicle includes a bounded World Events record with source, location,
-  time, weather, choice, and resolved outcome.
-- Fishing, mining, and foraging use stable location-derived nodes and distinct
-  bite/tension, strike/precision, and search/memory minigames. Eligibility uses
-  canonical terrain, location context, biome, time, weather, and node cooldowns.
-- Gathering outcomes are selected and saved before play so reload cannot reroll
-  rewards. Reduced motion replaces animation timing with deliberate steps while
-  preserving patterns, score thresholds, outcomes, and rewards.
-- Thirteen canonical fish, ores, gems, herbs, plants, wood, and relic materials
-  stack through normal inventory semantics, can be sold at bounded values, and
-  expose stable recipe-input metadata consumed directly by crafting recipes.
-  Rare guarded finds enter the normal Battle pipeline.
-- Fourteen data-driven recipes cover healing, cures, travel supplies, trap
-  tools, deterministic equipment upgrades, and rare elemental gear. Crafting
-  validates one selected hero or companion inventory, gold, batch size, station,
-  protected items, outputs, and equipment links before one atomic transaction.
-- Recipe discovery is idempotent across exploration, cities, quests, gathering,
-  shops, NPCs, readable lore, Codex knowledge, items, and World Events. Monster
-  drops, chests, shops, event rewards, and deterministic minor treasures provide
-  balanced canonical materials without replacing existing rewards.
-- 13 cities, including the optional island port Tidehaven, with connected districts, district-specific shops, gates,
-  discovery, fast travel, inns, banks, stables, and city music
-- Four multi-level dungeons with bidirectional stairs, floor-specific
-  encounters, chests, fog, procedural traps, and a unique deepest-floor boss
-- Seeded trap layouts with spike pits, poison darts, falling rocks, alarms,
-  hidden floors, and dungeon-specific runes; nearby checks use Dexterity or
-  Intelligence, detected traps can be disarmed for XP, and unresolved traps can
-  deal HP/MP damage, inflict combat statuses, summon encounters, or drop the
-  player to a deeper floor
-- Trap Kits, class talents, and Adventurer guidance improve detection and
-  disarming; seeded layouts and four-state trap outcomes persist explicitly
-- The seven-chapter **Twelvefold Covenant** main quest spans all 12 cities and
-  restores three keystones guarded by dungeon bosses, with two campaign

+## Highlights
+
+- **Create your hero:** choose from 12 classes, use 27-point buy or
+  4d6-drop-lowest stats, customize appearance, level to 20, and collect
+  equipment, talents, spells, abilities, and mounts.
+- **Complete a full campaign:** follow the Twelvefold Covenant through 12
+  mainland cities, three keystone dungeons, data-driven cutscenes, boss
+  encounters, an epilogue, and post-game continuation.
+- **Build a party:** recruit the Guardian, Scout, and Mystic; manage their
+  equipment and inventories; control them manually or automate turns with
+  ranked gambits.
+- **Fight tactical battles:** face groups of up to four enemies with initiative,
+  formations, ally and enemy targeting, nine elements, status effects, healing,
+  items, bosses, and full-party defeat recovery.
+- **Explore a changing world:** travel through connected city districts,
+  multi-level dungeons, seeded traps, fog of war, weather, day and night,
+  non-combat skill checks, World Events, and optional danger zones.
+- **Discover more than monsters:** expand the Codex with lore, make alignment
+  and reputation choices, earn achievements and cosmetic titles, and replay
+  unlocked story scenes in the Chronicle.
+- **Gather, craft, and sail:** fish, mine, forage, craft deterministic recipes
+  and equipment upgrades, use merchant routes, earn a boat, explore Tidehaven,
+  and challenge the Deepwake Kraken.

+  Accessibility settings include 100%/125%/150% text, high contrast, reduced

+## Browser and save support
+
+2D&D is designed for current desktop and mobile browsers. Release CI validates
+the game in Chromium; other current evergreen browsers are expected to work but
+are not part of the automated release gate. There is no desktop installer.

+Campaign saves, accessibility/audio settings, and inventory-view preferences
+are stored locally in the current browser profile. Saves do not automatically
+sync between browsers, devices, private windows, or cleared site data. The game
+has no account system, analytics, or server-side save service.

-- Normalized non-combat skill-check rolls, choices, and outcomes
-- Nautical boat ownership/condition/upgrades/cosmetics, discovered
-  ports/routes/islands/continents/sea tiles, bounded navigation statistics, and
-  recoverable pending merchant routes, hazards, and sea encounters
-- Recruited and active companion IDs; independent progression, resources,
-  inventories, equipment, status effects, dialogue state, control modes, and
-  normalized ranked gambit rules
-- New-player tutorial completion; pre-v9 campaigns migrate as already completed
-  so established saves are not interrupted
-- A stable World Event seed, roll/cooldown counters, one pending choice or
-  special encounter, idempotent resolved/claimed IDs, repeat counters, and a
-  bounded chronological event record
-- Bounded alignment axes, per-town and per-faction reputation scores, stable
-  applied source IDs, and a bounded recent-cause history. Alignment names,
-  reputation tiers, thresholds, shop modifiers, Codex milestones, and ending
-  variants are derived from canonical data
-- Achievement completion records, stable event counters/IDs, explicit defeat
-  history, unlocked/equipped cosmetic titles, debug exclusions, and queued
-  non-blocking notices. Definitions, categories, descriptions, points, totals,
-  and all safely reconstructable progress remain derived
-- A deterministic gathering seed, node cooldown/depletion state, discovered
-  nodes/resources, once-only claimed outcomes, per-discipline statistics,
-  bounded history, and an exact pending minigame or special encounter
-- Known recipe IDs, stable discovery and transaction IDs, natural craft and
-  equipment-upgrade statistics, per-recipe counts, and bounded recent history.
-  Recipe definitions, ingredient contracts, categories, and values are derived
-- Stable discovered feature IDs, queued one-time reveal feedback, explicit
-  debug reveals, and debug-suppressed evidence. Feature availability is
-  reconciled from authoritative quest, party, Codex, achievement, crafting,

-
-`loadGame()` migrates older flat player saves, normalizes new fields, and
-recovers invalid or conflicting world, city, and dungeon locations. Malformed
-skill-check records are discarded, while valid totals and outcomes are repaired.
-Schema-v3 skill-check saves gain default quest progress, and flat schema-v4
-Ashen Road saves migrate to the nested Covenant state without replaying rewards.
-Flat recruitment quest progress is migrated into the same nested log.
-Schema-v3 skill-check saves gain default trap progress, and schema-v4 quest
-saves gain default trap progress. Malformed trap seeds reset trap states
-so stale IDs cannot resolve against a different layout. Schema-v5 saves gain an
-empty party, and completed recruitment actions replay idempotently after party
-normalization. Older saves gain empty seen and pending cutscene lists; unknown,
-duplicate, malformed, or already-seen pending IDs are discarded. Migration
-queues only a completed-but-unseen campaign epilogue rather than replaying every
-historically eligible scene.
-Schema-v9 monster-only Codex saves gain an empty knowledge-ID collection, then
-recover deterministic unlocks from durable city, dungeon, item, quest, and
-cutscene evidence. Unknown, malformed, and duplicate knowledge IDs are removed
-without changing valid monster records.
-Schema-v10 and older saves gain default World Event state. Loading normalizes
-known event/choice IDs, bounds counters and records, rejects invalid locations,
-clears malformed pending encounters, and discards pending instances already
-present in the resolved record.
-Schema-v11 and older saves gain the Chaotic Neutral baseline with neutral
-reputation. Historical quest/event outcomes are not retroactively replayed;
-already-reached quest social source IDs are marked as consumed so existing
-quest, reward, Codex, and event state remains unchanged.
-Schema-v12 and older saves gain normalized achievement state and silently
-reconcile durable quest, boss, exploration, Codex, party, event, social, and
-inventory milestones. Legacy defeat history is deliberately marked unknown, so
-older completed campaigns cannot receive the no-defeat achievement by inference.
-Schema-v13 and older saves gain default gathering state. Schema-v14 loading
-normalizes stable IDs, statistics, cooldowns, history, and pending outcomes;
-replacing a malformed seed clears generated node state and pending play so
-rewards cannot resolve against an incompatible layout.
-Schema-v14 and older saves gain default crafting state. Schema-v15 removes
-unknown or duplicate recipe/discovery/transaction IDs, clamps statistics,
-repairs bounded history, preserves inventory/equipment links, and replays
-durable recipe discovery idempotently.
-Schema-v16 and older saves gain empty feature-discovery state, then silently
-reconcile every already-earned feature from durable gameplay evidence. Unknown,
-duplicate, malformed, pending, and debug-only IDs are removed so mature saves do
-not emit a storm of reveal notices.

1. # Companions and Gambits
2. 
3. [Documentation index](README.md) | [Gameplay](gameplay.md) |
4. [Architecture](architecture.md)
5. 
6. ## Party model
7. 
8. The persistent party was introduced in schema v6 and lives at `player.party` in
9. the current schema v17:
10. 
11. - `companions`: unique recruited `CompanionState` records
12. - `activeCompanionIds`: up to three recruited IDs in battle/follower order
13. 
14. The hero remains the owner of gold, bank balance, world position, mounts, and
15. world progression. Each companion owns independent XP, level, HP/MP, stats,
16. spells, abilities, talents, inventory, equipment, active effects, dialogue
17. cursor, control mode, and gambits.
18. 
19. The three stable companion IDs are:
20. 
21. | ID | Role | Class |
22. | --- | --- | --- |
23. | `guardian` | Defensive frontline | Paladin |
24. | `scout` | Mobile ranged damage | Ranger |
25. | `mystic` | Healing and party support | Cleric |
26. 
27. New recruits match the hero's current level using deterministic historical HP
28. and MP growth. Later XP and level-ups are independent.
29. 
30. ## Recruitment
31. 
32. Recruitment uses the canonical quest system:
33. 
34. - `recruitGuardian`
35. - `recruitScout`
36. - `recruitMystic`
37. 
38. Each quest has stable `meet*`, `*Trial`, and `*Oath` stage IDs and emits one
39. completion action:
40. 
41. ```text
42. companion.recruit.guardian
43. companion.recruit.scout
44. companion.recruit.mystic
45. ```
46. 
47. `replayQuestCompletionActions(..., "recruitCompanion")` runs after load,
48. Overworld initialization, NPC quest changes, and debug quest mutations.
49. `recruitCompanion()` is idempotent, so reloads, rewinds, and repeated debug
50. completion cannot duplicate a companion or starter inventory. Debug quest and
51. companion commands refresh the live follower sprites immediately.
52. 
53. ## Party management
54. 
55. Press `P` during exploration to open the party overlay.
56. 
57. The overlay supports:
58. 
59. - active/reserve membership and active order
60. - manual or gambit combat control
61. - member stats, HP/MP/XP, and equipment
62. - independent inventories and item transfer
63. - targeted consumables and healing outside combat
64. - pending companion stat allocation
65. - ranked gambit editing
66. 
67. The Items page uses immutable sorted and filtered views, full-text search,
68. procedural item visuals, and stable keyboard/pointer selection for large bags.
69. Its sort, filter, and search preferences are stored separately from actor
70. ownership. See [`inventory.md`](inventory.md) for controls and selector rules.
71. 
72. Key items, mounts, and equipped items cannot be transferred. Gold remains with
73. the hero; shop purchases and battle drops enter the hero bag and can then be
74. transferred.
75. 
76. ## Gambit rules
77. 
78. Each companion can store up to 12 enabled or disabled rules. Rank 1 has highest
79. priority.
80. 
81. The structured rule format is:
82. 
83. ```text
84. if [subject] has/is [condition] do [action] on [target]
85. ```
86. 
87. Supported subjects include self, hero, any party member, a specific companion,
88. and any enemy. Conditions cover HP/MP values or percentages, statuses,
89. alive/KO state, and ability-score comparisons. Actions cover attack, defend,
90. known spells, known abilities, and owned items. Targets include the matched
91. subject, named party members, lowest/highest HP allies or enemies, and
92. automatic area targets.
93. 
94. At the start of a gambit-controlled turn:
95. 
96. 1. Status start-of-turn processing resolves.
97. 2. Rules are evaluated by ascending rank against a fresh battle snapshot.
98. 3. Invalid targets, missing items, insufficient MP, consumed action slots, and
99.    inapplicable heals/buffs fall through without mutation.
100. 4. A valid bonus action may execute first.
101. 5. Lower-ranked rules continue until one main action executes.
102. 6. If no rule executes, the companion attacks; if no enemy is valid, it
103.    defends.
104. 
105. Manual companion turns and gambits both use `validateBattleAction()` and
106. `executeValidatedBattleAction()`.
107. 
108. ## Battle, KO, and rewards
109. 
110. Every conscious party member rolls initiative. Monsters select only living
111. party actors. Battle ends in defeat only when the whole active party is KO.
112. 
113. Living members receive victory XP. A member knocked out during the battle
114. receives no victory XP and loses progress earned toward the next level, down to
115. the current-level XP floor. A partially victorious KO member remains at 0 HP
116. until an inn.
117. 
118. On a full wipe:
119. 
120. - every active member receives the KO XP penalty
121. - the existing 30% hero-gold penalty applies once
122. - the party returns to the last town
123. - active members recover half HP/MP
124. - Battle effects are cleared and the recovered state is autosaved
125. - `DefeatScene` shows every defeated member, exact gold/XP losses, and the
126.   recovery location before continuing; boss and random encounters share this
127.   path
128. 
129. Inn rest revives and fully restores every recruited companion and processes
130. their pending level-ups.
131. 
132. ## Followers and world integration
133. 
134. Active conscious companions follow the hero using prior valid hero tiles. They
135. do not block movement or independently trigger traps, encounters, gates, or
136. world interactions. Pointer interaction talks directly to a follower; Space
137. uses companion dialogue only after higher-priority world interactions.
138. 
139. Dungeon movement preserves `DungeonTrapManager` ordering:
140. 
141. ```text
142. trap move/arrival handling -> exploration event -> random encounter
143. ```
144. 
145. Companions travel inside the existing `player` scene payload, so Battle, Shop,
146. Codex, fast travel, alarm encounters, and scene restarts preserve one party
147. state without a parallel transition field.
148. 
149. ## Debug commands
150. 
151. ```text
152. /companion list
153. /companion recruit <guardian|scout|mystic|all>
154. /companion mode <id> <manual|gambit>
155. /companion heal
156. /companion gambits <id>
157. ```
158. 
159. The debug MP hotkey is `O`; `P` is reserved for party management.
160.

Based on my review, I verified version numbers, schema versions, file paths, scene names, workflow steps, controls, debug commands, dependency versions, and links across the entire diff (README.md, AGENTS.md, all new `docs/*.md` files, modified skill files, and package.json/package-lock.json) against the actual source code. I found one genuine, verifiable omission:

## Issue: Documented debug capability silently dropped from all documentation
**File:** docs/development.md (Debug tools section, ~lines 60-87); previously documented in README.md (removed)
**Severity:** Low
**Problem:** The old README documented a working debug capability: forcing the next random encounter via a URL query parameter (`?forceGroup=<templateId>`, e.g. `?forceGroup=slimeSwarm`), implemented in `src/scenes/Overworld.ts` (`params.get("forceGroup")` / `params.delete("forceGroup")`). This capability still exists in the code but is no longer mentioned anywhere in the new documentation hierarchy (`docs/development.md`, `docs/testing.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, or `README.md`) — it has zero references after this change.
**Evidence:** `grep -rn "forceGroup" src/scenes/Overworld.ts` confirms the feature is live in code; `grep -rln "forceGroup" e2e/ tests/ docs/ AGENTS.md README.md .github/` returns no matches post-diff.
**Suggested fix:** Add a one-line mention of the `?forceGroup=` query parameter to `docs/development.md`'s debug tools section (it was previously called out alongside the slash commands) so the capability remains discoverable.

Everything else — including the schema/version claims, the documentation hierarchy restructuring, and preservation/reuse of `docs/companions.md` (only a nav line and an accurate schema-v6→v17 clarification were added, content otherwise untouched) — held up under verification.
